# Rosenblatt diagnostics and goodness-of-fit tests

This section implements a Rosenblatt goodness-of-fit test specifically for
the tensor-variate normal distribution. Suppose that

$$
\operatorname{vec}(\mathcal X_i)
\sim
N\left\{
  \operatorname{vec}(\mathcal M),
  \Sigma_D\otimes\cdots\otimes\Sigma_1
\right\}.
$$

If $\Sigma_d=L_dL_d^\top$, then the full Cholesky factor is the Kronecker
product of the mode-specific Cholesky factors. We therefore standardize each
draw without constructing the full covariance matrix:

$$
\mathcal Z_i =
(\mathcal X_i-\widehat{\mathcal M})
\times_1\widehat L_1^{-1}
\times_2\cdots
\times_D\widehat L_D^{-1}.
$$

Under a correctly specified model with known parameters, the entries of
$\mathcal Z_i$ are independent standard normals. Consequently,

$$
\mathcal U_i=\Phi(\mathcal Z_i)
$$

has independent Uniform$(0,1)$ entries. This is the Rosenblatt transform for
the coordinate ordering induced by the package's tensor vectorization.

Because the parameters are estimated from the same data being tested, the
usual reference distributions for goodness-of-fit statistics do not apply.
The implementation sections below derive the transformation and a refitted
parametric-bootstrap prototype. All runnable examples are consolidated in
**Step 9: Runnable Rosenblatt examples**. Run those example chunks in order.

## Step 1: Compute tensor-normal Rosenblatt residuals

The first function performs only the model fit and transformation. Its
`normal_scores` output contains the whitened tensors as an
$n\times p$ matrix, while `uniforms` contains their elementwise normal CDFs.
Rows represent tensor draws and columns follow the package's vectorization
order.

```{r tensor-normal-rosenblatt-transform}
tensor_normal_rosenblatt <- function(
    draws,
    fit = NULL,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL) {

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a `tensor` object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (n_draws(draws) < 2L) {
    stop("At least two tensor observations are required.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  tensor_dim <- draw_shape(draws)
  number_modes <- length(tensor_dim)
  p <- prod(tensor_dim)

  # Estimate the mean tensor and separable covariance factors unless the
  # caller has supplied an existing tensor-normal fit.
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    fit <- tensor_mle(
      draws,
      model = "normal",
      max_iter = max_iter,
      tol = tol,
      quiet = quiet,
      restrict = restrict
    )
  }

  if (is.null(fit$mu) ||
      is.null(fit$sigmas) ||
      length(fit$sigmas) != number_modes) {
    stop(
      "`fit` must contain `mu` and one covariance matrix per tensor mode.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (!identical(as.integer(dim(fit$mu)), as.integer(tensor_dim))) {
    stop(
      "The fitted mean and tensor observations have different dimensions.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # R's chol() returns an upper-triangular matrix R satisfying
  #
  #   Sigma = R' R.
  #
  # Thus L = R' is the lower-triangular factor and solve(L) is the required
  # whitening transformation.
  whitening_matrices <- vector("list", number_modes)

  for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
    sigma <- as.matrix(fit$sigmas[[mode]])

    if (!identical(dim(sigma), rep(tensor_dim[mode], 2L))) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "`fit$sigmas[[", mode, "]]` does not match tensor mode ",
          mode, "."
        ),
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }

    # Remove harmless numerical asymmetry before taking the Cholesky factor.
    sigma <- (sigma + t(sigma)) / 2

    lower_cholesky <- tryCatch(
      t(chol(sigma)),
      error = function(error) {
        stop(
          paste0(
            "The fitted covariance for mode ", mode,
            " is not positive definite."
          ),
          call. = FALSE
        )
      }
    )

    whitening_matrices[[mode]] <- solve(lower_cholesky)
  }

  normal_scores <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = n_draws(draws),
    ncol = p
  )

  for (i in seq_len(n_draws(draws))) {
    current <- pull_draw(draws, i) - fit$mu

    for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
      # Named arguments make the intended mode and matrix explicit.
      current <- n_prod(drop(unclass(current)), n = mode,  
                        mat = whitening_matrices[[mode]])
    }

    normal_scores[i, ] <- as.numeric(unclass(current))
  }

  uniforms <- pnorm(normal_scores)

  structure(
    list(
      normal_scores = normal_scores,
      uniforms = uniforms,
      fit = fit,
      tensor_dim = tensor_dim,
      whitening_matrices = whitening_matrices
    ),
    class = "tensor_normal_rosenblatt"
  )
}
```


## Step 2: Define complementary goodness-of-fit components

Checking only a pooled histogram of the uniforms is not sufficient: a wrong
model can produce approximately uniform marginal values that remain
dependent. The test therefore uses three components:

1. `marginal` applies an Anderson--Darling statistic to all Rosenblatt
   uniforms and emphasizes non-normal tails and marginal shape.
2. `radial` compares $\|\mathcal Z_i\|_F^2$ with its
   $\chi^2_p$ reference distribution.
3. `projection` examines many one-dimensional projections of the whitened
   tensors. Sparse, rank-one, and dense directions target different forms of
   residual dependence and non-normality.

```{r tensor-normal-rosenblatt-components}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2A. Anderson-Darling discrepancy for values that should be Uniform(0, 1)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

rosenblatt_ad_uniform <- function(uniform_values) {
  uniform_values <- as.numeric(uniform_values)

  if (!length(uniform_values) ||
      any(!is.finite(uniform_values))) {
    stop(
      "`uniform_values` must contain finite numeric values.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # pnorm() and pchisq() can round extreme values to exactly zero or one.
  # Clipping prevents log(0) without changing ordinary observations.
  clipping <- 1e-12
  uniform_values <- pmin(
    1 - clipping,
    pmax(clipping, uniform_values)
  )

  uniform_values <- sort(uniform_values)
  n <- length(uniform_values)
  index <- seq_len(n)

  -n - sum(
    (2 * index - 1) *
      (
        log(uniform_values) +
          log(1 - rev(uniform_values))
      )
  ) / n
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2B. Construct tensor-aware projection directions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_rosenblatt_directions <- function(
    tensor_dim,
    n_dense = 20L,
    n_rank_one = 20L,
    n_sparse = 20L,
    seed = NULL) {

  counts <- c(n_dense, n_rank_one, n_sparse)

  if (any(!is.finite(counts)) ||
      any(counts < 0) ||
      any(counts != floor(counts))) {
    stop(
      "The direction counts must be non-negative integers.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  n_dense <- as.integer(n_dense)
  n_rank_one <- as.integer(n_rank_one)
  n_sparse <- as.integer(n_sparse)

  if (sum(counts) == 0L) {
    stop("At least one projection direction is required.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  p <- prod(tensor_dim)
  number_modes <- length(tensor_dim)
  number_directions <- sum(counts)

  directions <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = number_directions,
    ncol = p
  )

  direction_type <- character(number_directions)
  current_direction <- 1L

  # Dense directions examine combinations of all tensor entries.
  if (n_dense > 0L) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_dense)) {
      direction <- rnorm(p)
      direction <- direction / sqrt(sum(direction^2))

      directions[current_direction, ] <- direction
      direction_type[current_direction] <- "dense"
      current_direction <- current_direction + 1L
    }
  }

  # Rank-one directions preserve the multilinear tensor structure:
  #
  #   a = a_1 outer a_2 outer ... outer a_D.
  if (n_rank_one > 0L) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_rank_one)) {
      mode_vectors <- lapply(
        tensor_dim,
        function(mode_size) {
          current_vector <- rnorm(mode_size)
          current_vector / sqrt(sum(current_vector^2))
        }
      )

      direction_array <- mode_vectors[[1L]]

      if (number_modes > 1L) {
        for (mode in 2:number_modes) {
          direction_array <- outer(
            direction_array,
            mode_vectors[[mode]]
          )
        }
      }

      direction <- as.numeric(direction_array)
      direction <- direction / sqrt(sum(direction^2))

      directions[current_direction, ] <- direction
      direction_type[current_direction] <- "rank_one"
      current_direction <- current_direction + 1L
    }
  }

  # Sparse directions examine individual tensor entries.
  if (n_sparse > 0L) {
    sparse_entries <- sample.int(
      p,
      size = n_sparse,
      replace = n_sparse > p
    )

    sparse_signs <- sample(
      c(-1, 1),
      size = n_sparse,
      replace = TRUE
    )

    for (j in seq_len(n_sparse)) {
      directions[
        current_direction,
        sparse_entries[j]
      ] <- sparse_signs[j]

      direction_type[current_direction] <- "sparse"
      current_direction <- current_direction + 1L
    }
  }

  rownames(directions) <- paste0(
    direction_type,
    "_",
    seq_len(number_directions)
  )

  attr(directions, "direction_type") <- direction_type
  directions
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2C. Calculate the three discrepancy components
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

tensor_normal_rosenblatt_components <- function(
    normal_scores,
    directions) {

  normal_scores <- as.matrix(normal_scores)
  directions <- as.matrix(directions)

  n <- nrow(normal_scores)
  p <- ncol(normal_scores)

  if (n < 2L || p < 1L) {
    stop(
      "`normal_scores` must contain at least two rows.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (ncol(directions) != p || nrow(directions) < 1L) {
    stop(
      "`directions` must have one column per tensor entry.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  direction_lengths <- sqrt(rowSums(directions^2))

  if (any(!is.finite(direction_lengths)) ||
      any(direction_lengths <= 0)) {
    stop("Every projection direction must be nonzero.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # Normalize user-supplied directions as well as generated directions.
  directions <- directions / direction_lengths

  # Component 1: all entries should be marginally standard normal, or
  # equivalently their CDF values should be Uniform(0, 1).
  marginal_statistic <- rosenblatt_ad_uniform(
    pnorm(normal_scores)
  )

  # Component 2: each complete whitened tensor should have squared Frobenius
  # norm distributed as chi-squared with p degrees of freedom.
  radial_distances <- rowSums(normal_scores^2)

  radial_statistic <- rosenblatt_ad_uniform(
    pchisq(radial_distances, df = p)
  )

  # Component 3: every unit-length projection should be standard normal.
  projected_scores <- normal_scores %*% t(directions)

  projection_statistics <- apply(
    projected_scores,
    2,
    function(current_projection) {
      rosenblatt_ad_uniform(
        pnorm(current_projection)
      )
    }
  )

  projection_statistic <- max(projection_statistics)

  list(
    components = c(
      marginal = marginal_statistic,
      radial = radial_statistic,
      projection = projection_statistic
    ),
    radial_distances = radial_distances,
    projection_statistics = projection_statistics,
    projected_scores = projected_scores
  )
}
```

## Step 3: Run the refitted parametric-bootstrap test

The complete test first fits the observed tensors. It then holds the
projection directions fixed while repeatedly simulating and refitting the
tensor-normal model. The three components have different numerical scales,
so each is standardized using its bootstrap null distribution. The global
statistic is the largest of the three standardized discrepancies.

```{r tensor-normal-rosenblatt-bootstrap}
gof_tensor_normal_rosenblatt <- function(
    draws,
    B = 199L,
    directions = NULL,
    n_dense = 20L,
    n_rank_one = 20L,
    n_sparse = 20L,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    seed = NULL,
    show_progress = TRUE) {

  data_name <- deparse(substitute(draws))

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a `tensor` object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (length(B) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(B) ||
      B != floor(B) ||
      B < 19L) {
    stop(
      "`B` must be one integer greater than or equal to 19.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  B <- as.integer(B)

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  n <- n_draws(draws)
  tensor_dim <- draw_shape(draws)

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3A. Fit and transform the observed tensor sample
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  observed_rosenblatt <- tensor_normal_rosenblatt(
    draws = draws,
    max_iter = max_iter,
    tol = tol,
    quiet = quiet,
    restrict = restrict
  )

  observed_fit <- observed_rosenblatt$fit

  # Generate the directions once. Holding them fixed ensures that the
  # observed and bootstrap datasets are evaluated in exactly the same ways.
  if (is.null(directions)) {
    directions <- make_rosenblatt_directions(
      tensor_dim = tensor_dim,
      n_dense = n_dense,
      n_rank_one = n_rank_one,
      n_sparse = n_sparse
    )
  } else {
    directions <- as.matrix(directions)
  }

  observed_details <- tensor_normal_rosenblatt_components(
    normal_scores = observed_rosenblatt$normal_scores,
    directions = directions
  )

  observed_components <- observed_details$components

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3B. Simulate, refit, and transform every bootstrap sample
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  bootstrap_components <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = length(observed_components),
    dimnames = list(
      NULL,
      names(observed_components)
    )
  )

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    bootstrap_draws <- rtnorm(
      n = n,
      mu = observed_fit$mu,
      sigmas = observed_fit$sigmas
    )

    bootstrap_result <- tryCatch(
      {
        bootstrap_fit <- tensor_mle(
          bootstrap_draws,
          model = "normal",
          max_iter = max_iter,
          tol = tol,
          quiet = quiet,
          restrict = restrict
        )

        bootstrap_rosenblatt <- tensor_normal_rosenblatt(
          draws = bootstrap_draws,
          fit = bootstrap_fit
        )

        tensor_normal_rosenblatt_components(
          normal_scores = bootstrap_rosenblatt$normal_scores,
          directions = directions
        )$components
      },
      error = function(error) NULL
    )

    if (!is.null(bootstrap_result) &&
        all(is.finite(bootstrap_result))) {
      bootstrap_components[b, ] <- bootstrap_result
    }

    if (show_progress &&
        (b %% 25L == 0L || b == B)) {
      message(
        "Completed ",
        b,
        " of ",
        B,
        " Rosenblatt bootstrap samples."
      )
    }
  }

  successful <- apply(
    bootstrap_components,
    1,
    function(current_row) {
      all(is.finite(current_row))
    }
  )

  number_successful <- sum(successful)
  number_failed <- B - number_successful

  if (number_successful < 10L) {
    stop(
      "Fewer than 10 bootstrap fits succeeded.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (number_failed > 0L) {
    warning(
      number_failed,
      " of ",
      B,
      " bootstrap fits failed. The p-values use the ",
      number_successful,
      " successful fits.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  successful_components <- bootstrap_components[
    successful,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3C. Put the components on comparable scales and form the global statistic
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  component_center <- colMeans(successful_components)
  component_scale <- apply(successful_components, 2, sd)

  if (any(!is.finite(component_scale)) ||
      any(component_scale <= 0)) {
    stop(
      "A bootstrap component has zero or non-finite variation.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  observed_standardized <- (
    observed_components -
      component_center
  ) / component_scale

  bootstrap_standardized <- sweep(
    successful_components,
    2,
    component_center,
    "-"
  )

  bootstrap_standardized <- sweep(
    bootstrap_standardized,
    2,
    component_scale,
    "/"
  )

  observed_global <- max(observed_standardized)
  bootstrap_global <- apply(bootstrap_standardized, 1, max)

  global_p_value <- (
    1 + sum(bootstrap_global >= observed_global)
  ) / (
    number_successful + 1
  )

  component_p_values <- vapply(
    names(observed_components),
    function(component_name) {
      (
        1 + sum(
          successful_components[, component_name] >=
            observed_components[component_name]
        )
      ) / (
        number_successful + 1
      )
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  structure(
    list(
      statistic = c(T = observed_global),
      parameter = c(
        successful_bootstrap_replicates = number_successful
      ),
      p.value = global_p_value,
      method = paste(
        "Parametric-bootstrap Rosenblatt test for",
        "the tensor-variate normal distribution"
      ),
      data.name = data_name,
      alternative = "the fitted tensor-normal model is misspecified",
      fit = observed_fit,
      normal_scores = observed_rosenblatt$normal_scores,
      uniforms = observed_rosenblatt$uniforms,
      component_statistics = observed_components,
      standardized_components = observed_standardized,
      component_p_values = component_p_values,
      radial_distances = observed_details$radial_distances,
      projection_statistics =
        observed_details$projection_statistics,
      directions = directions,
      bootstrap_components = bootstrap_components,
      bootstrap_statistics = bootstrap_global,
      component_center = component_center,
      component_scale = component_scale,
      bootstrap_failures = number_failed
    ),
    class = "htest"
  )
}
```

## Step 4: Interpreting bootstrap components

The runnable normal and skew-
\(t\) examples are collected in Step 9 so that no example depends on an object
defined many pages earlier. The refitted bootstrap can take considerable time;
use a small `B` only while checking code and at least 999 successful replicates
for a reported analysis.

Interpret the global p-value first. The component p-values are diagnostic:

- A small `marginal` p-value suggests incorrect marginal shape, skewness, or
  tails after whitening.
- A small `radial` p-value suggests incorrect tensor-level tail or scale
  behavior.
- A small `projection` p-value suggests remaining dependence or non-normality
  along one or more tensor directions.

These component p-values are not intended as three independent hypothesis
tests. The global p-value already accounts for selecting the largest
standardized discrepancy.

# Rosenblatt extension for the skewed tensor distributions

The skew-\(t\), variance-gamma, inverse-Gaussian, and generalized-hyperbolic
models all have the normal variance--mean mixture representation

$$
\mathcal X=\mathcal M+W\mathcal A+\sqrt W\,\mathcal Z.
$$

After mode-wise whitening, entry \(j\) has the conditional model

$$
Y_j\mid W\sim N(WB_j,W).
$$

All four mixing distributions are GIG distributions or GIG limits. If the
current conditional distribution of \(W\) is
\(\operatorname{GIG}(\lambda_j,\chi_j,\psi_j)\), the Rosenblatt coordinate is

$$
U_j=\int_0^\infty
\Phi\left\{\frac{Y_j-WB_j}{\sqrt W}\right\}
f_{\mathrm{GIG}}(W;\lambda_j,\chi_j,\psi_j)\,dW.
$$

After observing \(Y_j\), conjugacy gives

$$
\lambda_{j+1}=\lambda_j-\frac12,\quad
\chi_{j+1}=\chi_j+Y_j^2,\quad
\psi_{j+1}=\psi_j+B_j^2.
$$

Thus the test needs one shared univariate conditional CDF, not four different
high-dimensional tensor CDFs.

## Step 5: Starting GIG parameters and the shared conditional CDF

```{r tensor-skewed-rosenblatt-cdf}
rosenblatt_gig_parameters <- function(
    fit,
    model = c("skewt", "vargamma", "invgauss", "genhyper")) {

  model <- match.arg(model)

  if (model == "skewt") {
    if (is.null(fit$nu) || !is.finite(fit$nu) || fit$nu <= 0) {
      stop("The skew-t fit must contain a positive `nu`.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    return(c(lambda = -fit$nu / 2, chi = fit$nu, psi = 0))
  }

  if (model == "vargamma") {
    if (is.null(fit$gamma) ||
        !is.finite(fit$gamma) ||
        fit$gamma <= 0) {
      stop(
        "The variance-gamma fit must contain a positive `gamma`.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
    return(c(
      lambda = fit$gamma,
      chi = 0,
      psi = 2 * fit$gamma
    ))
  }

  if (model == "invgauss") {
    if (is.null(fit$kappa) ||
        !is.finite(fit$kappa) ||
        fit$kappa <= 0) {
      stop(
        "The inverse-Gaussian fit must contain a positive `kappa`.",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
    return(c(
      lambda = -1 / 2,
      chi = 1,
      psi = fit$kappa^2
    ))
  }

  if (is.null(fit$lambda) ||
      is.null(fit$omega) ||
      !is.finite(fit$lambda) ||
      !is.finite(fit$omega) ||
      fit$omega <= 0) {
    stop(
      "The generalized-hyperbolic fit requires finite `lambda` and ",
      "positive `omega`.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  c(
    lambda = fit$lambda,
    chi = fit$omega,
    psi = fit$omega
  )
}


p_normal_mean_variance_mixture <- function(
    q,
    beta,
    lambda,
    chi,
    psi,
    rel_tol = 1e-6,
    abs_tol = 1e-10,
    subdivisions = 100L) {

  if (length(q) != 1L ||
      anyNA(c(q, beta, lambda, chi, psi)) ||
      any(!is.finite(c(beta, lambda, chi, psi)))) {
    stop("The mixture CDF requires scalar finite parameters.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (chi < 0 || psi < 0 || (chi == 0 && psi == 0)) {
    stop(
      "GIG parameters require non-negative `chi` and `psi`, not both zero.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (q == -Inf) return(0)
  if (q == Inf) return(1)
  if (!is.finite(q)) stop("`q` must be finite or infinite.", call. = FALSE)

  subdivisions <- as.integer(subdivisions)

  if (length(subdivisions) != 1L ||
      is.na(subdivisions) ||
      subdivisions < 20L) {
    stop("`subdivisions` must be an integer of at least 20.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!is.finite(rel_tol) ||
      !is.finite(abs_tol) ||
      rel_tol <= 0 ||
      abs_tol < 0) {
    stop("The integration tolerances are invalid.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  integrand <- function(w) {
    answer <- numeric(length(w))
    positive <- is.finite(w) & w > 0

    if (any(positive)) {
      current_w <- w[positive]
      answer[positive] <- pnorm(
        (q - beta * current_w) / sqrt(current_w)
      ) * GIGrvg::dgig(
        current_w,
        lambda = lambda,
        chi = chi,
        psi = psi
      )
    }

    answer
  }

  integral <- integrate(
    integrand,
    lower = 0,
    upper = Inf,
    rel.tol = rel_tol,
    abs.tol = abs_tol,
    subdivisions = subdivisions,
    stop.on.error = FALSE
  )

  if (!is.finite(integral$value)) {
    stop("The mixture CDF integration failed.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!identical(integral$message, "OK")) {
    stop(
      "The mixture CDF integration did not converge: ",
      integral$message,
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  pmin(1, pmax(0, integral$value))
}
```

The starting parameterizations are:

- skew-\(t\): \(\operatorname{GIG}(-\nu/2,\nu,0)\);
- variance-gamma: \(\operatorname{GIG}(\gamma,0,2\gamma)\);
- inverse-Gaussian: \(\operatorname{GIG}(-1/2,1,\kappa^2)\);
- generalized hyperbolic:
  \(\operatorname{GIG}(\lambda,\omega,\omega)\).

## Step 6: Sequential skewed Rosenblatt transform

The output `whitened_values` contains \(Y_j\), while `uniforms` contains the
actual sequential Rosenblatt coordinates. The `normal_scores` output is
\(\Phi^{-1}(U_j)\), which lets us reuse the marginal, radial, and projection
statistics from the normal section.

```{r tensor-skewed-rosenblatt-transform}
tensor_skewed_rosenblatt <- function(
    draws,
    model = c("skewt", "vargamma", "invgauss", "genhyper"),
    fit = NULL,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    cdf_rel_tol = 1e-6,
    cdf_abs_tol = 1e-10,
    cdf_subdivisions = 100L) {

  model <- match.arg(model)

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor") || n_draws(draws) < 2L) {
    stop(
      "`draws` must be a tensor object with at least two observations.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (is.null(fit)) {
    fit <- tensor_mle(
      draws,
      model = model,
      max_iter = max_iter,
      tol = tol,
      quiet = quiet,
      restrict = restrict
    )
  }

  if (is.null(fit$skew)) {
    stop("The fitted skewed model must contain `skew`.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # The normal helper supplies exactly the required mode-wise whitening.
  whitened <- tensor_normal_rosenblatt(draws, fit = fit)
  whitened_values <- whitened$normal_scores
  whitened_skew <- fit$skew

  for (mode in seq_along(whitened$whitening_matrices)) {
    whitened_skew <- n_prod(
      whitened_skew,
      n = mode,
      mat = whitened$whitening_matrices[[mode]]
    )
  }

  beta <- as.numeric(unclass(whitened_skew))
  starting_gig <- rosenblatt_gig_parameters(fit, model)

  uniforms <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = nrow(whitened_values),
    ncol = ncol(whitened_values)
  )

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(whitened_values))) {
    lambda_current <- starting_gig["lambda"]
    chi_current <- starting_gig["chi"]
    psi_current <- starting_gig["psi"]

    for (j in seq_len(ncol(whitened_values))) {
      y_current <- whitened_values[i, j]
      beta_current <- beta[j]

      uniforms[i, j] <- p_normal_mean_variance_mixture(
        q = y_current,
        beta = beta_current,
        lambda = lambda_current,
        chi = chi_current,
        psi = psi_current,
        rel_tol = cdf_rel_tol,
        abs_tol = cdf_abs_tol,
        subdivisions = cdf_subdivisions
      )

      lambda_current <- lambda_current - 1 / 2
      chi_current <- chi_current + y_current^2
      psi_current <- psi_current + beta_current^2
    }
  }

  clipping <- 1e-12
  normal_scores <- matrix(
    qnorm(
      pmin(1 - clipping, pmax(clipping, uniforms))
    ),
    nrow = nrow(uniforms),
    ncol = ncol(uniforms)
  )

  list(
    normal_scores = normal_scores,
    uniforms = uniforms,
    whitened_values = whitened_values,
    whitened_skew = beta,
    fit = fit,
    model = model,
    tensor_dim = draw_shape(draws),
    starting_gig = starting_gig
  )
}
```

## Step 7: Simulate from a fitted model

```{r tensor-rosenblatt-model-helpers}
simulate_fitted_rosenblatt_model <- function(
    n,
    fit,
    model = c(
      "normal", "skewt", "vargamma", "invgauss", "genhyper"
    )) {

  model <- match.arg(model)

  switch(
    model,
    normal = rtnorm(n, fit$mu, fit$sigmas),
    skewt = rtskewt(
      n, fit$mu, fit$sigmas, fit$skew, fit$nu
    ),
    vargamma = rtvargamma(
      n, fit$mu, fit$sigmas, fit$skew, fit$gamma
    ),
    invgauss = rtinvgauss(
      n, fit$mu, fit$sigmas, fit$skew, fit$kappa
    ),
    genhyper = rtgenhyper(
      n, fit$mu, fit$skew, fit$sigmas, fit$lambda, fit$omega
    )
  )
}


transform_fitted_rosenblatt_model <- function(
    draws,
    fit,
    model,
    cdf_rel_tol,
    cdf_abs_tol,
    cdf_subdivisions) {

  if (model == "normal") {
    return(tensor_normal_rosenblatt(draws, fit = fit))
  }

  tensor_skewed_rosenblatt(
    draws = draws,
    model = model,
    fit = fit,
    cdf_rel_tol = cdf_rel_tol,
    cdf_abs_tol = cdf_abs_tol,
    cdf_subdivisions = cdf_subdivisions
  )
}
```

## Step 8: One bootstrap GOF interface for all five models

```{r tensor-all-models-rosenblatt-bootstrap}
gof_tensor_rosenblatt <- function(
    draws,
    model = c(
      "normal", "skewt", "vargamma", "invgauss", "genhyper"
    ),
    B = 199L,
    directions = NULL,
    n_dense = 20L,
    n_rank_one = 20L,
    n_sparse = 20L,
    fit = NULL,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    cdf_rel_tol = 1e-6,
    cdf_abs_tol = 1e-10,
    cdf_subdivisions = 100L,
    seed = NULL,
    show_progress = TRUE) {

  model <- match.arg(model)
  data_name <- deparse(substitute(draws))

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a tensor object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (length(B) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(B) ||
      B != floor(B) ||
      B < 19L) {
    stop("`B` must be an integer of at least 19.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  B <- as.integer(B)
  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)

  observed_fit <- fit

  if (is.null(observed_fit)) {
    observed_fit <- tensor_mle(
      draws,
      model = model,
      max_iter = max_iter,
      tol = tol,
      quiet = quiet,
      restrict = restrict
    )
  }

  observed_transform <- transform_fitted_rosenblatt_model(
    draws,
    observed_fit,
    model,
    cdf_rel_tol,
    cdf_abs_tol,
    cdf_subdivisions
  )

  if (is.null(directions)) {
    directions <- make_rosenblatt_directions(
      draw_shape(draws),
      n_dense,
      n_rank_one,
      n_sparse
    )
  }

  observed_details <- tensor_normal_rosenblatt_components(
    observed_transform$normal_scores,
    directions
  )
  observed_components <- observed_details$components

  bootstrap_components <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = length(observed_components),
    dimnames = list(NULL, names(observed_components))
  )

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    current_components <- tryCatch(
      {
        bootstrap_draws <- simulate_fitted_rosenblatt_model(
          n_draws(draws),
          observed_fit,
          model
        )

        bootstrap_fit <- tensor_mle(
          bootstrap_draws,
          model = model,
          max_iter = max_iter,
          tol = tol,
          quiet = quiet,
          restrict = restrict
        )

        bootstrap_transform <- transform_fitted_rosenblatt_model(
          bootstrap_draws,
          bootstrap_fit,
          model,
          cdf_rel_tol,
          cdf_abs_tol,
          cdf_subdivisions
        )

        tensor_normal_rosenblatt_components(
          bootstrap_transform$normal_scores,
          directions
        )$components
      },
      error = function(error) NULL
    )

    if (!is.null(current_components) &&
        all(is.finite(current_components))) {
      bootstrap_components[b, ] <- current_components
    }

    if (show_progress && (b %% 10L == 0L || b == B)) {
      message("Completed ", b, " of ", B, " ", model, " bootstraps.")
    }
  }

  successful <- apply(
    bootstrap_components,
    1,
    function(x) all(is.finite(x))
  )
  number_successful <- sum(successful)
  number_failed <- B - number_successful

  if (number_successful < 10L) {
    stop("Fewer than 10 bootstrap replicates succeeded.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (number_failed > 0L) {
    warning(
      number_failed,
      " bootstrap fits or transforms failed; inference uses ",
      number_successful,
      " successful replicates.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  successful_components <- bootstrap_components[
    successful,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  component_center <- colMeans(successful_components)
  component_scale <- apply(successful_components, 2, sd)

  if (any(!is.finite(component_scale)) ||
      any(component_scale <= 0)) {
    stop("A bootstrap component has no finite variation.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  observed_standardized <- (
    observed_components - component_center
  ) / component_scale

  bootstrap_standardized <- sweep(
    successful_components,
    2,
    component_center,
    "-"
  )
  bootstrap_standardized <- sweep(
    bootstrap_standardized,
    2,
    component_scale,
    "/"
  )

  observed_global <- max(observed_standardized)
  bootstrap_global <- apply(bootstrap_standardized, 1, max)
  global_p_value <- (
    1 + sum(bootstrap_global >= observed_global)
  ) / (
    number_successful + 1
  )

  component_p_values <- vapply(
    names(observed_components),
    function(component) {
      (
        1 + sum(
          successful_components[, component] >=
            observed_components[component]
        )
      ) / (
        number_successful + 1
      )
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  structure(
    list(
      statistic = c(T = observed_global),
      parameter = c(
        successful_bootstrap_replicates = number_successful
      ),
      p.value = global_p_value,
      method = paste(
        "Parametric-bootstrap Rosenblatt test for the tensor-variate",
        model,
        "distribution"
      ),
      data.name = data_name,
      alternative = paste("the fitted", model, "model is misspecified"),
      model = model,
      fit = observed_fit,
      uniforms = observed_transform$uniforms,
      normal_scores = observed_transform$normal_scores,
      component_statistics = observed_components,
      standardized_components = observed_standardized,
      component_p_values = component_p_values,
      radial_distances = observed_details$radial_distances,
      projection_statistics = observed_details$projection_statistics,
      directions = directions,
      bootstrap_components = bootstrap_components,
      bootstrap_statistics = bootstrap_global,
      bootstrap_failures = number_failed
    ),
    class = "htest"
  )
}
```

## Step 9: Runnable Rosenblatt examples

This is the only example section for the Rosenblatt transformation. The chunks
are self-contained as a group and should be run in order. They use the current
exported package functions rather than reimplementing the conditional CDF in
the analysis file.

### Example 1: Simulate normal and skew-\(t\) tensor observations

Both samples use the same \(2\times3\) tensor shape, location, and separable
covariance factors. The skew-\(t\) sample additionally uses a skew tensor and
degrees of freedom \(\nu=7\).

```{r rosenblatt-example-data}
set.seed(2)

rosenblatt_dims <- c(2L, 3L)

rosenblatt_mu <- array(
  c(-0.3, -0.1, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7),
  dim = rosenblatt_dims
)

rosenblatt_sigmas <- list(
  matrix(c(1.0, 0.35, 0.35, 0.8), nrow = 2),
  toeplitz(0.45^(0:2))
)

rosenblatt_skew <- array(
  c(0.4, -0.2, 0.3, 0, 0.15, -0.1),
  dim = rosenblatt_dims
)

rosenblatt_nu <- 7
rosenblatt_n <- 100

rosenblatt_normal_draws <- rtnorm(
  n = rosenblatt_n,
  mu = rosenblatt_mu,
  sigmas = rosenblatt_sigmas
)

rosenblatt_skewt_draws <- rtskewt(
  n = rosenblatt_n,
  mu = rosenblatt_mu,
  sigmas = rosenblatt_sigmas,
  skew = rosenblatt_skew,
  nu = rosenblatt_nu
)
```

### Example 2: Transform using known parameters

Known parameters are useful for validating the transformation. Under the
generating model, all returned entries should be independent Uniform\((0,1)\).
The output remains a `tensor` object with the same number and shape of draws.

```{r rosenblatt-known-parameter-transforms}
rosenblatt_normal_known <- tensor_rosenblatt(
  draws = rosenblatt_normal_draws,
  model = "normal",
  parameters = list(
    mu = rosenblatt_mu,
    sigmas = rosenblatt_sigmas
  )
)

rosenblatt_skewt_known <- tensor_rosenblatt(
  draws = rosenblatt_skewt_draws,
  model = "skewt",
  parameters = list(
    mu = rosenblatt_mu,
    skew = rosenblatt_skew,
    sigmas = rosenblatt_sigmas,
    nu = rosenblatt_nu
  )
)

c(
  normal_min = min(unclass(rosenblatt_normal_known)),
  normal_max = max(unclass(rosenblatt_normal_known)),
  skewt_min = min(unclass(rosenblatt_skewt_known)),
  skewt_max = max(unclass(rosenblatt_skewt_known))
)
```

For the skew-\(t\) model, `rosenblatt_tskewt()` is a convenience wrapper around
the second call above. Use whichever interface reads more clearly in the
surrounding analysis; it is unnecessary to run both.

### Example 3: Plot the main diagnostics

The helper below produces three plots:

1. a histogram, which should be approximately flat;
2. a uniform Q--Q plot, which should follow the diagonal;
3. a radial Q--Q plot based on
   \(\sum_j\{\Phi^{-1}(U_{ij})\}^2\), which should follow
   \(\chi^2_p\) when parameters are known.

```{r rosenblatt-diagnostic-helper}
rosenblatt_matrix <- function(uniform_tensor) {
  matrix(
    as.numeric(unclass(uniform_tensor)),
    nrow = n_draws(uniform_tensor),
    ncol = prod(draw_shape(uniform_tensor))
  )
}

plot_rosenblatt_diagnostics <- function(uniform_tensor, label) {
  uniforms <- rosenblatt_matrix(uniform_tensor)
  clipping <- 1e-12
  normal_scores <- matrix(
    qnorm(pmin(1 - clipping, pmax(clipping, uniforms))),
    nrow = nrow(uniforms),
    ncol = ncol(uniforms)
  )
  radial_distances <- rowSums(normal_scores^2)

  old_par <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
  on.exit(par(old_par), add = TRUE)

  hist(
    as.numeric(uniforms),
    breaks = 20,
    probability = TRUE,
    main = paste(label, "histogram"),
    xlab = "Rosenblatt value",
    ylim = c(0, 1.4)
  )
  abline(h = 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

  qqplot(
    ppoints(length(uniforms)),
    sort(as.numeric(uniforms)),
    main = paste(label, "uniform Q-Q"),
    xlab = "Theoretical uniform quantiles",
    ylab = "Observed quantiles"
  )
  abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

  qqplot(
    qchisq(ppoints(nrow(uniforms)), df = ncol(uniforms)),
    sort(radial_distances),
    main = paste(label, "radial Q-Q"),
    xlab = "Theoretical chi-squared quantiles",
    ylab = "Observed radial distances"
  )
  abline(a = 0, b = 1, col = "red", lwd = 2)

  invisible(list(
    uniforms = uniforms,
    normal_scores = normal_scores,
    radial_distances = radial_distances
  ))
}
```

```{r rosenblatt-known-parameter-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}
normal_diagnostics <- plot_rosenblatt_diagnostics(
  rosenblatt_normal_known,
  label = "Tensor normal"
)

skewt_diagnostics <- plot_rosenblatt_diagnostics(
  rosenblatt_skewt_known,
  label = "Tensor skew-t"
)
```

### Example 4: Transform using fitted skew-\(t\) parameters

In an application, fit the model once and pass the fitted list directly to
`tensor_rosenblatt()`. These residuals remain valuable graphically, but they
are not exact independent uniforms because the same observations estimated the
parameters.

```{r rosenblatt-fitted-skewt}
rosenblatt_skewt_fit <- tensor_mle(
  rosenblatt_skewt_draws,
  model = "skewt",
  quiet = TRUE
)

rosenblatt_skewt_fitted <- tensor_rosenblatt(
  draws = rosenblatt_skewt_draws,
  model = "skewt",
  parameters = rosenblatt_skewt_fit
)

rosenblatt_skewt_fit$nu
```

```{r rosenblatt-fitted-skewt-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=4}
fitted_skewt_diagnostics <- plot_rosenblatt_diagnostics(
  rosenblatt_skewt_fitted,
  label = "Fitted tensor skew-t"
)
```

### Example 5: Obtain a formal multiplier-calibrated test

`tensor_gof_scores()` accounts for fitted parameters using analytic scores and
a weighted multiplier calibration. It is much faster than repeatedly fitting
bootstrap tensor samples. `B = 199` is adequate for checking the workflow;
increase it to at least 1999 for a reported p-value. Keep the score dimension
and basis dimension small relative to the number of tensor observations.

```{r rosenblatt-multiplier-test}
rosenblatt_skewt_gof <- tensor_gof_scores(
  draws = rosenblatt_skewt_draws,
  model = "skewt",
  fit = rosenblatt_skewt_fit,
  marginal_degree = 2,
  include_interactions = TRUE,
  max_basis = 20,
  calibration = "multiplier",
  B = 199,
  seed = 2026
)

rosenblatt_skewt_gof

c(
  score_dimension = rosenblatt_skewt_gof$score_dimension,
  information_rank = rosenblatt_skewt_gof$information_rank,
  basis_rank = rosenblatt_skewt_gof$adjusted_covariance_rank
)
```

Do not substitute `tensor_score_gof()` here: that older function uses the
experimental asymptotic chi-squared calibration. The multiplier calibration in
`tensor_gof_scores()` is the preferred package implementation.

### Example 6: Optional full parametric bootstrap

The earlier `gof_tensor_rosenblatt()` prototype in this document simulates,
refits, and retransforms every bootstrap dataset. It is statistically direct
but substantially slower. This chunk is deliberately not evaluated when the
document is knitted. Run it interactively with a small `B`, then use at least
999 successful replicates for a reported result.

```{r rosenblatt-full-bootstrap, eval=FALSE}
rosenblatt_skewt_bootstrap_quick <- gof_tensor_rosenblatt(
  draws = rosenblatt_skewt_draws,
  model = "skewt",
  B = 19,
  seed = 2026
)

rosenblatt_skewt_bootstrap_quick
rosenblatt_skewt_bootstrap_quick$component_p_values

# Final analysis:
# rosenblatt_skewt_bootstrap_final <- gof_tensor_rosenblatt(
#   draws = rosenblatt_skewt_draws,
#   model = "skewt",
#   B = 999,
#   seed = 2026
# )
```

### Model-specific parameter names

The same `tensor_rosenblatt()` interface supports all five package models:

| `model` | Additional entries in `parameters` |
|:--|:--|
| `"normal"` | none beyond `mu` and `sigmas` |
| `"skewt"` | `skew`, `nu` |
| `"vargamma"` | `skew`, `gamma` (or `scale`) |
| `"invgauss"` | `skew`, `kappa` |
| `"genhyper"` | `skew`, `lambda`, `omega` |

The skewed transforms require one numerical integral per tensor entry. For
large tensors, first compute and inspect the residual diagnostics. A full
refitted bootstrap may be impractical, and a score-adjusted formal test is not
reliable when its nuisance-score dimension approaches or exceeds the number of
tensor observations.

# Simple parameter-adjusted characteristic-function test

The functions in this section implement the test in small, separate steps.
The main quantities are:

$$s_i(\widehat\theta) = \nabla_\theta \log f(X_i;\widehat\theta), \qquad \widehat I = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_i s_i^\top$$

and

$$\widehat C = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \{g(X_i)-\bar g\}\{s_i-\bar s\}^\top,$$

where \(g(X_i)\) contains the cosine and sine characteristic-function
features. The fitted-parameter correction removes the part of these features
that is explained by the likelihood scores.

```{r simple-adjusted-characteristic-functions}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Create characteristic-function frequencies
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_cf_frequencies <- function(tensor_dim,
                                n_directions = 5L,
                                radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
                                seed = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  p <- prod(tensor_dim)
  number_frequencies <- n_directions * length(radii)
  frequencies <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = number_frequencies,
    ncol = p
  )

  current_row <- 1L

  for (radius in radii) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_directions)) {
      # Draw a direction and rescale it to have length one.
      direction <- rnorm(p)
      direction <- direction / sqrt(sum(direction^2))

      # The radius determines how far from zero the frequency lies.
      frequencies[current_row, ] <- radius * direction
      current_row <- current_row + 1L
    }
  }

  frequencies
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Standardize every tensor observation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

standardize_cf_draws <- function(draws, fit) {
  n <- n_draws(draws)
  p <- prod(draw_shape(draws))
  number_modes <- length(draw_shape(draws))

  # W_d Sigma_d W_d' = I for each tensor mode.
  whitening <- vector("list", number_modes)

  for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
    sigma <- as.matrix(fit$sigmas[[mode]])
    sigma <- (sigma + t(sigma)) / 2
    whitening[[mode]] <- solve(t(chol(sigma)))
  }

  standardized <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = p)

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    current <- pull_draw(draws, i) - fit$mu

    for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
      current <- n_prod(current, mode, whitening[[mode]])
    }

    standardized[i, ] <- as.numeric(unclass(current))
  }

  standardized
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Evaluate the theoretical CF of the standardized fitted model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

theoretical_standardized_cf <- function(
    frequencies,
    fit,
    model = c(
      "normal",
      "skewt",
      "vargamma",
      "invgauss",
      "genhyper"
    )) {

  model <- match.arg(model)
  frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)

  # q_j = ||t_j||^2 for the standardized observations.
  q <- rowSums(frequencies^2)

  if (model == "normal") {
    return(as.complex(exp(-q / 2)))
  }

  # The skew tensor must be transformed by the same whitening matrices used
  # for the observations.
  whitened_skew <- fit$skew

  for (mode in seq_along(fit$sigmas)) {
    sigma <- as.matrix(fit$sigmas[[mode]])
    sigma <- (sigma + t(sigma)) / 2
    whitening <- solve(t(chol(sigma)))
    whitened_skew <- n_prod(whitened_skew, mode, whitening)
  }

  whitened_skew <- as.numeric(whitened_skew)
  skew_projection <- drop(frequencies %*% whitened_skew)

  # All four skewed models have the standardized representation
  #
  #     Z = W * skew + sqrt(W) * epsilon.
  #
  # Their CF is the Laplace transform of W evaluated at this complex value.
  s <- q / 2 - 1i * skew_projection

  if (model == "skewt") {
    shape <- fit$nu / 2
    rate <- fit$nu / 2
    answer <- complex(length(s))
    at_zero <- Mod(s) < sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
    answer[at_zero] <- 1 + 0i

    if (any(!at_zero)) {
      current_s <- s[!at_zero]
      argument <- 2 * sqrt(rate * current_s)

      # BesselK(..., expon.scaled = TRUE) returns exp(argument) K(argument).
      log_bessel <- log(Bessel::BesselK(
        argument,
        nu = shape,
        expon.scaled = TRUE
      )) - argument

      answer[!at_zero] <- exp(
        log(2) +
          (shape / 2) * (log(rate) + log(current_s)) -
          lgamma(shape) +
          log_bessel
      )
    }

    return(answer)
  }

  if (model == "vargamma") {
    return((fit$gamma / (fit$gamma + s))^fit$gamma)
  }

  if (model == "invgauss") {
    return(exp(
      fit$kappa *
        (1 - sqrt(1 + 2 * s / fit$kappa^2))
    ))
  }

  # Generalized-hyperbolic mixing distribution.
  shifted_psi <- fit$omega + 2 * s
  argument <- sqrt(fit$omega * shifted_psi)

  log_numerator_bessel <- log(Bessel::BesselK(
    argument,
    nu = fit$lambda,
    expon.scaled = TRUE
  )) - argument

  log_denominator_bessel <- log(Bessel::BesselK(
    fit$omega,
    nu = fit$lambda,
    expon.scaled = TRUE
  )) - fit$omega

  exp(
    (fit$lambda / 2) *
      (log(fit$omega) - log(shifted_psi)) +
      log_numerator_bessel -
      log_denominator_bessel
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. List every free parameter direction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_score_directions <- function(
    fit,
    model,
    tensor_dim,
    restrict = NULL) {

  p <- prod(tensor_dim)
  number_modes <- length(tensor_dim)
  directions <- list()

  # There is one location parameter for every entry of the mean tensor.
  for (j in seq_len(p)) {
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "mu",
      index = j,
      name = paste0("mu[", j, "]"),
      scale = max(1, abs(as.numeric(fit$mu)[j]))
    )
  }

  # Every non-normal model has one skew parameter per tensor entry.
  if (model != "normal") {
    for (j in seq_len(p)) {
      directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
        type = "skew",
        index = j,
        name = paste0("skew[", j, "]"),
        scale = max(1, abs(as.numeric(fit$skew)[j]))
      )
    }
  }

  # A restricted normal covariance factor is fixed and has no score direction.
  fixed_modes <- integer(0)

  if (model == "normal" && length(restrict)) {
    fixed_modes <- as.integer(restrict)
  }

  for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
    if (mode %in% fixed_modes) {
      next
    }

    mode_size <- tensor_dim[mode]
    sigma <- as.matrix(fit$sigmas[[mode]])
    sigma_scale <- max(1, sqrt(mean(sigma^2)))

    if (mode < number_modes) {
      # The package fixes the trace of the first D - 1 covariance factors.
      # E_jj - E_pp changes two diagonal values but leaves the trace unchanged.
      if (mode_size > 1L) {
        for (row in seq_len(mode_size - 1L)) {
          direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
          direction_matrix[row, row] <- 1
          direction_matrix[mode_size, mode_size] <- -1

          directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
            type = "sigma",
            mode = mode,
            matrix = direction_matrix,
            name = paste0(
              "sigma", mode, "_diag_contrast_", row
            ),
            scale = sigma_scale
          )
        }
      }
    } else {
      # The last covariance factor carries the unrestricted overall scale.
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size)) {
        direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
        direction_matrix[row, row] <- 1

        directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
          type = "sigma",
          mode = mode,
          matrix = direction_matrix,
          name = paste0("sigma", mode, "_diag_", row),
          scale = sigma_scale
        )
      }
    }

    # One symmetric direction for each free off-diagonal covariance entry.
    if (mode_size > 1L) {
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size - 1L)) {
        for (column in seq.int(row + 1L, mode_size)) {
          direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
          direction_matrix[row, column] <- 1
          direction_matrix[column, row] <- 1

          directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
            type = "sigma",
            mode = mode,
            matrix = direction_matrix,
            name = paste0(
              "sigma", mode, "_offdiag_", row, "_", column
            ),
            scale = sigma_scale
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  # Positive mixing parameters are perturbed on the logarithmic scale.
  if (model == "skewt") {
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_nu",
      name = "log(nu)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  if (model == "vargamma") {
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_gamma",
      name = "log(gamma)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  if (model == "invgauss") {
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_kappa",
      name = "log(kappa)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  if (model == "genhyper") {
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "lambda",
      name = "lambda",
      scale = max(1, abs(fit$lambda))
    )

    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_omega",
      name = "log(omega)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  directions
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Move the fitted model in one parameter direction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

perturb_fit_in_direction <- function(
    fit,
    direction,
    amount,
    tensor_dim) {

  candidate <- fit

  if (direction$type == "mu") {
    value <- as.numeric(candidate$mu)
    value[direction$index] <- value[direction$index] + amount
    candidate$mu <- array(value, dim = tensor_dim)
  }

  if (direction$type == "skew") {
    value <- as.numeric(candidate$skew)
    value[direction$index] <- value[direction$index] + amount
    candidate$skew <- array(value, dim = tensor_dim)
  }

  if (direction$type == "sigma") {
    mode <- direction$mode
    candidate$sigmas[[mode]] <-
      candidate$sigmas[[mode]] +
      amount * direction$matrix

    candidate$sigmas[[mode]] <-
      (candidate$sigmas[[mode]] +
         t(candidate$sigmas[[mode]])) / 2
  }

  if (direction$type == "log_nu") {
    candidate$nu <- fit$nu * exp(amount)
  }

  if (direction$type == "log_gamma") {
    candidate$gamma <- fit$gamma * exp(amount)
  }

  if (direction$type == "log_kappa") {
    candidate$kappa <- fit$kappa * exp(amount)
  }

  if (direction$type == "lambda") {
    candidate$lambda <- fit$lambda + amount
  }

  if (direction$type == "log_omega") {
    candidate$omega <- fit$omega * exp(amount)
  }

  candidate
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Evaluate one log likelihood per observation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

model_log_density <- function(draws, fit, model) {
  switch(
    model,
    normal = dtnorm(
      draws,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      log = TRUE
    ),
    skewt = dtskewt(
      draws,
      mu = fit$mu,
      skew = fit$skew,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      nu = fit$nu,
      log = TRUE
    ),
    vargamma = dtvargamma(
      draws,
      mu = fit$mu,
      skew = fit$skew,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      scale = fit$gamma,
      log = TRUE
    ),
    invgauss = dtinvgauss(
      draws,
      mu = fit$mu,
      skew = fit$skew,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      kappa = fit$kappa,
      log = TRUE
    ),
    genhyper = dtgenhyper(
      draws,
      mu = fit$mu,
      skew = fit$skew,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      lambda = fit$lambda,
      omega = fit$omega,
      log = TRUE
    )
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Estimate the likelihood score matrix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

estimate_score_matrix <- function(
    draws,
    fit,
    model,
    restrict = NULL,
    finite_difference = 1e-5) {

  n <- n_draws(draws)
  tensor_dim <- draw_shape(draws)

  directions <- make_score_directions(
    fit = fit,
    model = model,
    tensor_dim = tensor_dim,
    restrict = restrict
  )

  number_parameters <- length(directions)
  scores <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n,
    ncol = number_parameters
  )
  parameter_names <- character(number_parameters)

  for (parameter in seq_len(number_parameters)) {
    direction <- directions[[parameter]]
    parameter_names[parameter] <- direction$name

    # Central finite difference:
    #
    #   score = {log f(theta + h) - log f(theta - h)} / (2h).
    step <- finite_difference * direction$scale
    derivative_found <- FALSE

    # A covariance factor may be close to its positive-definite boundary.
    # If necessary, make the numerical step smaller.
    for (attempt in seq_len(12L)) {
      fit_plus <- perturb_fit_in_direction(
        fit,
        direction,
        amount = step,
        tensor_dim = tensor_dim
      )

      fit_minus <- perturb_fit_in_direction(
        fit,
        direction,
        amount = -step,
        tensor_dim = tensor_dim
      )

      covariance_ok <- TRUE

      if (direction$type == "sigma") {
        mode <- direction$mode

        plus_cholesky <- try(
          chol(fit_plus$sigmas[[mode]]),
          silent = TRUE
        )
        minus_cholesky <- try(
          chol(fit_minus$sigmas[[mode]]),
          silent = TRUE
        )

        covariance_ok <-
          !inherits(plus_cholesky, "try-error") &&
          !inherits(minus_cholesky, "try-error")
      }

      if (covariance_ok) {
        log_plus <- tryCatch(
          model_log_density(draws, fit_plus, model),
          error = function(error) rep(NA_real_, n)
        )

        log_minus <- tryCatch(
          model_log_density(draws, fit_minus, model),
          error = function(error) rep(NA_real_, n)
        )

        if (all(is.finite(log_plus)) && all(is.finite(log_minus))) {
          scores[, parameter] <-
            (log_plus - log_minus) / (2 * step)

          derivative_found <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }

      step <- step / 2
    }

    if (!derivative_found) {
      stop(
        "Could not estimate the score for ",
        direction$name,
        ".",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
  }

  colnames(scores) <- parameter_names
  scores
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Estimate the CF gradient term
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

estimate_cf_gradient <- function(feature_matrix, score_matrix) {
  n <- nrow(feature_matrix)

  centered_features <- sweep(
    feature_matrix,
    2,
    colMeans(feature_matrix),
    "-"
  )

  centered_scores <- sweep(
    score_matrix,
    2,
    colMeans(score_matrix),
    "-"
  )

  # This is Cov{g(X), score(X)}. Under the MLE information identity it
  # supplies the gradient term in the fitted-parameter CF correction.
  crossprod(centered_features, centered_scores) / n
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Compute the fitted-parameter corrected covariance matrix
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

compute_corrected_cf_covariance <- function(
    feature_matrix,
    score_matrix,
    information_tolerance = 1e-8) {

  n <- nrow(feature_matrix)

  centered_features <- sweep(
    feature_matrix,
    2,
    colMeans(feature_matrix),
    "-"
  )

  centered_scores <- sweep(
    score_matrix,
    2,
    colMeans(score_matrix),
    "-"
  )

  # Outer-product estimate of Fisher information.
  information <- crossprod(centered_scores) / n
  information <- (information + t(information)) / 2

  # Use only identifiable information directions.
  information_eigen <- eigen(
    information,
    symmetric = TRUE
  )

  cutoff <- max(information_eigen$values, 0) *
    information_tolerance

  keep <- information_eigen$values > cutoff

  if (!any(keep)) {
    stop(
      "The estimated information matrix has rank zero.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  kept_vectors <- information_eigen$vectors[
    , keep, drop = FALSE
  ]

  inverse_information <- kept_vectors %*%
    diag(
      1 / information_eigen$values[keep],
      nrow = sum(keep)
    ) %*%
    t(kept_vectors)

  cf_gradient <- estimate_cf_gradient(
    feature_matrix,
    score_matrix
  )

  # Remove the portion of every CF feature explained by MLE estimation.
  fitted_parameter_part <- centered_scores %*%
    inverse_information %*%
    t(cf_gradient)

  adjusted_features <-
    centered_features - fitted_parameter_part

  corrected_covariance <-
    crossprod(adjusted_features) / n

  corrected_covariance <-
    (corrected_covariance + t(corrected_covariance)) / 2

  list(
    covariance = corrected_covariance,
    information = information,
    inverse_information = inverse_information,
    information_rank = sum(keep),
    cf_gradient = cf_gradient,
    adjusted_features = adjusted_features
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Perform the complete characteristic-function GOF test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gof_characteristic_adjusted <- function(
    draws,
    model = c(
      "normal",
      "skewt",
      "vargamma",
      "invgauss",
      "genhyper"
    ),
    frequencies = NULL,
    n_directions = 5L,
    radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
    n_mixture = 100000L,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    finite_difference = 1e-5,
    information_tolerance = 1e-8,
    eigen_tolerance = 1e-10,
    seed = NULL) {

  model <- match.arg(model)
  data_name <- deparse(substitute(draws))

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a tensor object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  # Fit the model once. No bootstrap samples are fitted.
  fit <- tensor_mle(
    draws,
    model = model,
    max_iter = max_iter,
    tol = tol,
    quiet = quiet,
    restrict = restrict
  )

  if (is.null(frequencies)) {
    frequencies <- make_cf_frequencies(
      tensor_dim = draw_shape(draws),
      n_directions = n_directions,
      radii = radii
    )
  } else {
    frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)
  }

  n <- n_draws(draws)
  number_frequencies <- nrow(frequencies)

  # Each row contains one standardized tensor observation.
  standardized <- standardize_cf_draws(draws, fit)

  # The phase matrix has one row per observation and one column per frequency.
  phases <- standardized %*% t(frequencies)

  # These are the real and imaginary components of exp(i t'X).
  feature_matrix <- cbind(
    cos(phases),
    sin(phases)
  )

  empirical_cf <- colMeans(exp(1i * phases))

  theoretical_cf <- theoretical_standardized_cf(
    frequencies = frequencies,
    fit = fit,
    model = model
  )

  cf_difference <- empirical_cf - theoretical_cf

  test_statistic <- n * mean(
    Mod(cf_difference)^2
  )

  # Estimate one likelihood-score column for every free fitted parameter.
  score_matrix <- estimate_score_matrix(
    draws = draws,
    fit = fit,
    model = model,
    restrict = restrict,
    finite_difference = finite_difference
  )

  correction <- compute_corrected_cf_covariance(
    feature_matrix = feature_matrix,
    score_matrix = score_matrix,
    information_tolerance = information_tolerance
  )

  # The statistic averages over frequencies, so divide the covariance by L.
  all_eigenvalues <- eigen(
    correction$covariance / number_frequencies,
    symmetric = TRUE,
    only.values = TRUE
  )$values

  eigenvalue_cutoff <- max(all_eigenvalues, 0) *
    eigen_tolerance

  eigenvalues <- all_eigenvalues[
    all_eigenvalues > eigenvalue_cutoff
  ]

  if (!length(eigenvalues)) {
    stop(
      "The corrected covariance matrix has rank zero.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # Simulate the limiting weighted chi-squared distribution.
  mixture_statistics <- numeric(n_mixture)

  for (j in seq_along(eigenvalues)) {
    mixture_statistics <- mixture_statistics +
      eigenvalues[j] * rchisq(n_mixture, df = 1)
  }

  p_value <- (
    1 + sum(mixture_statistics >= test_statistic)
  ) / (
    n_mixture + 1
  )

  structure(
    list(
      statistic = c(T = test_statistic),
      p.value = p_value,
      method = paste(
        "Parameter-adjusted characteristic-function test for",
        model
      ),
      data.name = data_name,
      model = model,
      fit = fit,
      frequencies = frequencies,
      empirical_cf = empirical_cf,
      theoretical_cf = theoretical_cf,
      score_matrix = score_matrix,
      cf_gradient = correction$cf_gradient,
      information = correction$information,
      information_rank = correction$information_rank,
      corrected_covariance = correction$covariance,
      eigenvalues = eigenvalues,
      all_eigenvalues = all_eigenvalues,
      mixture_statistics = mixture_statistics
    ),
    class = "htest"
  )
}
```

# Independent-reference parameter correction

The function above estimates its covariance correction from the same tensors
used to calculate the test statistic. The functions below instead generate a
large, independent sample from the fitted model. The model is still fitted only
once. The independent sample is used only to estimate the null covariance and
its eigenvalues.

```{r independent-reference-characteristic-test}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Simulate tensors from any of the five fitted models
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

simulate_cf_reference_draws <- function(
    n,
    fit,
    model = c(
      "normal",
      "skewt",
      "vargamma",
      "invgauss",
      "genhyper"
    )) {

  model <- match.arg(model)

  # Each model uses the parameter names returned by tensor_mle().
  if (model == "normal") {
    return(rtnorm(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas
    ))
  }

  if (model == "skewt") {
    return(rtskewt(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      skew = fit$skew,
      nu = fit$nu
    ))
  }

  if (model == "vargamma") {
    return(rtvargamma(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      skew = fit$skew,
      scale = fit$gamma
    ))
  }

  if (model == "invgauss") {
    return(rtinvgauss(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      skew = fit$skew,
      kappa = fit$kappa
    ))
  }

  rtgenhyper(
    n = n,
    mu = fit$mu,
    sigmas = fit$sigmas,
    skew = fit$skew,
    lambda = fit$lambda,
    omega = fit$omega
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Estimate the corrected covariance using an independent sample
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

estimate_reference_cf_covariance <- function(
    reference_draws,
    fit,
    model,
    frequencies,
    restrict = NULL,
    finite_difference = 1e-5,
    information_tolerance = 1e-8) {

  M <- n_draws(reference_draws)
  frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)
  L <- nrow(frequencies)

  # Standardize the reference tensors using the fitted parameters from the
  # observed data. The model is not fitted again.
  standardized_reference <- standardize_cf_draws(
    draws = reference_draws,
    fit = fit
  )

  # phases[i, j] is the tensor inner product between reference tensor i and
  # frequency tensor j after standardization.
  phases <- standardized_reference %*% t(frequencies)

  # There are two real features for each frequency: cosine and sine.
  reference_features <- cbind(
    cos(phases),
    sin(phases)
  )

  theoretical_cf <- theoretical_standardized_cf(
    frequencies = frequencies,
    fit = fit,
    model = model
  )

  theoretical_feature_mean <- c(
    Re(theoretical_cf),
    Im(theoretical_cf)
  )

  # G contains the centered CF features
  #
  #   cos(t'X) - Re{phi(t)}
  #   sin(t'X) - Im{phi(t)}.
  #
  # We subtract the known theoretical means rather than the reference-sample
  # means.
  G <- sweep(
    reference_features,
    2,
    theoretical_feature_mean,
    "-"
  )

  # Estimate the likelihood score for every reference tensor. This evaluates
  # the density at nearby parameter values but does not run tensor_mle().
  S <- estimate_score_matrix(
    draws = reference_draws,
    fit = fit,
    model = model,
    restrict = restrict,
    finite_difference = finite_difference
  )

  # A population likelihood score has mean zero. Subtracting its small
  # simulation mean reduces Monte Carlo noise.
  S <- sweep(
    S,
    2,
    colMeans(S),
    "-"
  )

  # V is the covariance of the unadjusted cosine and sine features.
  V <- crossprod(G) / M
  V <- (V + t(V)) / 2

  # I is an outer-product estimate of Fisher information.
  information <- crossprod(S) / M
  information <- (information + t(information)) / 2

  # C measures how each CF feature moves with each estimated parameter.
  C <- crossprod(G, S) / M

  # Numerically invert only the identifiable directions of the information
  # matrix. This is a transparent pseudoinverse.
  information_eigen <- eigen(
    information,
    symmetric = TRUE
  )

  information_cutoff <- max(
    information_eigen$values,
    0
  ) * information_tolerance

  keep_information <- information_eigen$values >
    information_cutoff

  if (!any(keep_information)) {
    stop(
      "The reference information matrix has rank zero.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  kept_vectors <- information_eigen$vectors[
    , keep_information, drop = FALSE
  ]

  inverse_information <- kept_vectors %*%
    diag(
      1 / information_eigen$values[keep_information],
      nrow = sum(keep_information)
    ) %*%
    t(kept_vectors)

  # This is the fitted-parameter correction:
  #
  #   V_corrected = V - C I^{-1} C'.
  #
  # It removes the CF variation that is absorbed by estimating the MLE.
  parameter_part <- C %*%
    inverse_information %*%
    t(C)

  corrected_covariance <- V - parameter_part
  corrected_covariance <- (
    corrected_covariance + t(corrected_covariance)
  ) / 2

  list(
    covariance = corrected_covariance,
    unadjusted_covariance = V,
    parameter_part = parameter_part,
    cf_gradient = C,
    information = information,
    inverse_information = inverse_information,
    information_rank = sum(keep_information),
    n_reference = M,
    n_frequencies = L
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Run the complete independent-reference CF goodness-of-fit test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gof_characteristic_reference <- function(
    draws,
    model = c(
      "normal",
      "skewt",
      "vargamma",
      "invgauss",
      "genhyper"
    ),
    frequencies = NULL,
    n_directions = 5L,
    radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
    n_reference = 10000L,
    n_mixture = 100000L,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    finite_difference = 1e-5,
    information_tolerance = 1e-8,
    eigen_tolerance = 1e-10,
    seed = NULL) {

  model <- match.arg(model)
  data_name <- deparse(substitute(draws))

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a tensor object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  n_reference <- as.integer(n_reference)
  n_mixture <- as.integer(n_mixture)

  if (n_reference < 2L) {
    stop("`n_reference` must be at least 2.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (n_mixture < 1L) {
    stop("`n_mixture` must be positive.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Observed-data portion
  # ---------------------------------------------------------

  # Fit the chosen model exactly once.
  fit <- tensor_mle(
    draws,
    model = model,
    max_iter = max_iter,
    tol = tol,
    quiet = quiet,
    restrict = restrict
  )

  if (is.null(frequencies)) {
    frequencies <- make_cf_frequencies(
      tensor_dim = draw_shape(draws),
      n_directions = n_directions,
      radii = radii
    )
  } else {
    frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)
  }

  n <- n_draws(draws)
  L <- nrow(frequencies)

  standardized_observed <- standardize_cf_draws(
    draws = draws,
    fit = fit
  )

  observed_phases <- standardized_observed %*%
    t(frequencies)

  empirical_cf <- colMeans(
    exp(1i * observed_phases)
  )

  theoretical_cf <- theoretical_standardized_cf(
    frequencies = frequencies,
    fit = fit,
    model = model
  )

  cf_difference <- empirical_cf - theoretical_cf

  # This statistic uses only the original observed tensors.
  test_statistic <- n * mean(
    Mod(cf_difference)^2
  )

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Independent-reference portion
  # ---------------------------------------------------------

  # Generate one large independent sample under the fitted null model.
  # These tensors are not used to change the observed test statistic.
  reference_draws <- simulate_cf_reference_draws(
    n = n_reference,
    fit = fit,
    model = model
  )

  # Estimate V, C, and I from the independent tensors.
  correction <- estimate_reference_cf_covariance(
    reference_draws = reference_draws,
    fit = fit,
    model = model,
    frequencies = frequencies,
    restrict = restrict,
    finite_difference = finite_difference,
    information_tolerance = information_tolerance
  )

  # T_n averages its squared discrepancies over L frequencies, so the
  # mixture weights are the eigenvalues of V_corrected / L.
  all_eigenvalues <- eigen(
    correction$covariance / L,
    symmetric = TRUE,
    only.values = TRUE
  )$values

  eigenvalue_cutoff <- max(
    all_eigenvalues,
    0
  ) * eigen_tolerance

  eigenvalues <- all_eigenvalues[
    all_eigenvalues > eigenvalue_cutoff
  ]

  if (!length(eigenvalues)) {
    stop(
      "The reference corrected covariance has rank zero.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  # Simulate the weighted chi-squared limiting distribution
  #
  #   lambda[1] chi-square[1] + ... + lambda[r] chi-square[r].
  #
  # This loop generates scalar chi-squares, not tensor-valued bootstrap data.
  mixture_statistics <- numeric(n_mixture)

  for (j in seq_along(eigenvalues)) {
    mixture_statistics <- mixture_statistics +
      eigenvalues[j] * rchisq(n_mixture, df = 1)
  }

  # The p-value is the upper-tail probability. The add-one adjustment avoids
  # returning exactly zero when the statistic exceeds every simulated value.
  p_value <- (
    1 + sum(mixture_statistics >= test_statistic)
  ) / (
    n_mixture + 1
  )

  structure(
    list(
      statistic = c(T = test_statistic),
      p.value = p_value,
      method = paste(
        "Independent-reference parameter-adjusted CF test for",
        model
      ),
      data.name = data_name,
      model = model,
      fit = fit,
      frequencies = frequencies,
      empirical_cf = empirical_cf,
      theoretical_cf = theoretical_cf,
      n_reference = n_reference,
      unadjusted_covariance = correction$unadjusted_covariance,
      parameter_part = correction$parameter_part,
      cf_gradient = correction$cf_gradient,
      information = correction$information,
      information_rank = correction$information_rank,
      corrected_covariance = correction$covariance,
      eigenvalues = eigenvalues,
      all_eigenvalues = all_eigenvalues,
      mixture_statistics = mixture_statistics
    ),
    class = "htest"
  )
}
```

For example, the tensor-normal test is:

```{r independent-reference-example, eval=FALSE}
tic()
result <- gof_characteristic_reference(
  draws = norm_draws,
  model = "normal",
  n_reference = 1000,
  seed = 123
)
toc()
```


```{r}


result$statistic
result$p.value
```

Only the `model` argument changes for the skewed distributions:

```{r independent-reference-model-names, eval=FALSE}
normal_result <- gof_characteristic_reference(draws, model = "normal")
skewt_result <- gof_characteristic_reference(draws, model = "skewt")
vargamma_result <- gof_characteristic_reference(draws, model = "vargamma")
invgauss_result <- gof_characteristic_reference(draws, model = "invgauss")
genhyper_result <- gof_characteristic_reference(draws, model = "genhyper")
```

# Simple parametric-bootstrap characteristic-function test

This version directly approximates the null distribution by repeatedly
simulating and refitting the selected model. It is slower than the eigenvalue
methods, but its steps closely match the definition of a parametric bootstrap.

```{r simple-parametric-bootstrap-characteristic-test}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Calculate the CF distance for one fitted model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_fitted_cf_statistic <- function(
    draws,
    fit,
    model,
    frequencies) {

  n <- n_draws(draws)
  frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)

  # Standardize every observation with the parameters from this fit.
  standardized <- standardize_cf_draws(
    draws = draws,
    fit = fit
  )

  # Each entry is the inner product between one standardized tensor and one
  # frequency tensor.
  phases <- standardized %*% t(frequencies)

  # Average exp(i t'X) over observations to obtain the empirical CF.
  empirical_cf <- colMeans(
    exp(1i * phases)
  )

  # Evaluate the theoretical CF under this fitted model.
  theoretical_cf <- theoretical_standardized_cf(
    frequencies = frequencies,
    fit = fit,
    model = model
  )

  # The test statistic is the average squared CF distance, multiplied by n:
  #
  #   T = n * mean(|empirical CF - theoretical CF|^2).
  squared_distance <- Mod(
    empirical_cf - theoretical_cf
  )^2

  list(
    statistic = n * mean(squared_distance),
    empirical_cf = empirical_cf,
    theoretical_cf = theoretical_cf,
    squared_distance = squared_distance
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Perform the complete parametric-bootstrap test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gof_characteristic_bootstrap <- function(
    draws,
    model = c(
      "normal",
      "skewt",
      "vargamma",
      "invgauss",
      "genhyper"
    ),
    B = 1000L,
    frequencies = NULL,
    n_directions = 5L,
    radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    seed = NULL,
    show_progress = TRUE) {

  model <- match.arg(model)
  data_name <- deparse(substitute(draws))

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a tensor object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  B <- as.integer(B)

  if (B < 1L) {
    stop("`B` must be positive.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  n <- n_draws(draws)

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Observed-data portion
  # ---------------------------------------------------------

  # Fit the selected model to the observed tensors.
  observed_fit <- tensor_mle(
    draws,
    model = model,
    max_iter = max_iter,
    tol = tol,
    quiet = quiet,
    restrict = restrict
  )

  # Create the frequencies once. Exactly the same frequencies are used for
  # the observed data and every bootstrap sample.
  if (is.null(frequencies)) {
    frequencies <- make_cf_frequencies(
      tensor_dim = draw_shape(draws),
      n_directions = n_directions,
      radii = radii
    )
  } else {
    frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)
  }

  # Calculate the observed distance between the empirical and fitted CFs.
  observed <- calculate_fitted_cf_statistic(
    draws = draws,
    fit = observed_fit,
    model = model,
    frequencies = frequencies
  )

  # ---------------------------------------------------------
  # Bootstrap portion
  # ---------------------------------------------------------

  bootstrap_statistics <- rep(
    NA_real_,
    B
  )

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    # One bootstrap dataset contains n tensors, not one tensor. It is
    # generated from the model fitted to the original observations.
    bootstrap_draws <- simulate_cf_reference_draws(
      n = n,
      fit = observed_fit,
      model = model
    )

    # Refitting is essential. It makes the bootstrap reproduce the effect of
    # estimating the parameters before calculating the CF discrepancy.
    bootstrap_fit <- tryCatch(
      tensor_mle(
        bootstrap_draws,
        model = model,
        max_iter = max_iter,
        tol = tol,
        quiet = quiet,
        restrict = restrict
      ),
      error = function(error) NULL
    )

    # A skewed-model optimization can occasionally fail. Leave this replicate
    # as NA and continue rather than losing all completed bootstrap work.
    if (!is.null(bootstrap_fit)) {
      bootstrap_result <- tryCatch(
        calculate_fitted_cf_statistic(
          draws = bootstrap_draws,
          fit = bootstrap_fit,
          model = model,
          frequencies = frequencies
        ),
        error = function(error) NULL
      )

      if (!is.null(bootstrap_result) &&
          is.finite(bootstrap_result$statistic)) {
        bootstrap_statistics[b] <-
          bootstrap_result$statistic
      }
    }

    if (show_progress &&
        (b %% 25L == 0L || b == B)) {
      message(
        "Completed ",
        b,
        " of ",
        B,
        " bootstrap samples."
      )
    }
  }

  successful <- is.finite(
    bootstrap_statistics
  )

  number_successful <- sum(successful)
  number_failed <- B - number_successful

  if (number_successful == 0L) {
    stop(
      "Every bootstrap model fit failed.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (number_failed > 0L) {
    warning(
      number_failed,
      " of ",
      B,
      " bootstrap model fits failed. The p-value uses the ",
      number_successful,
      " successful fits.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  successful_statistics <- bootstrap_statistics[
    successful
  ]

  # Large CF distances are evidence against the fitted model. Therefore the
  # p-value is the upper-tail proportion of bootstrap statistics.
  p_value <- (
    1 + sum(
```
