```{r simple-parametric-bootstrap-characteristic-test}
      successful_statistics >= observed$statistic
    )
  ) / (
    number_successful + 1
  )

  structure(
    list(
      statistic = c(T = observed$statistic),
      p.value = p_value,
      method = paste(
        "Parametric-bootstrap characteristic-function test for",
        model
      ),
      data.name = data_name,
      model = model,
      fit = observed_fit,
      frequencies = frequencies,
      empirical_cf = observed$empirical_cf,
      theoretical_cf = observed$theoretical_cf,
      squared_distance = observed$squared_distance,
      bootstrap_statistics = bootstrap_statistics,
      B = B,
      successful_bootstraps = number_successful,
      failed_bootstraps = number_failed
    ),
    class = "htest"
  )
}
```

For a quick trial, use a small `B`. For the final analysis, change it to
`B = 1000`.

```{r simple-parametric-bootstrap-example, eval=FALSE}
# A quick check while developing the analysis
quick_result <- gof_characteristic_bootstrap(
  draws = norm_draws,
  model = "normal",
  B = 49,
  seed = 123
)

# The requested final bootstrap analysis
bootstrap_result <- gof_characteristic_bootstrap(
  draws = norm_draws,
  model = "normal",
  B = 1000,
  seed = 123
)

bootstrap_result$statistic
bootstrap_result$p.value
```

# Omnibus tensor characteristic-function test

The preceding test averages the raw CF discrepancies across frequencies. That
average can lose power when a model is wrong in only a few tensor directions.
The following version uses several kinds of tensor frequencies, standardizes
the discrepancy at each frequency, and records the largest discrepancy. It
also includes a radial statistic that is sensitive to unusually light or
heavy tails.

The final p-value is obtained by a parametric bootstrap. Consequently, every
bootstrap dataset is refitted and the complete statistic is recalculated.

```{r omnibus-characteristic-bootstrap-test}
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Generate several scientifically useful kinds of tensor frequencies
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

make_omnibus_cf_frequencies <- function(
    tensor_dim,
    n_dense = 25L,
    n_rank_one = 25L,
    n_sparse = 25L,
    radii = c(0.5, 1, 2),
    seed = NULL) {

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  p <- prod(tensor_dim)
  number_modes <- length(tensor_dim)
  number_directions <-
    n_dense + n_rank_one + n_sparse

  directions <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = number_directions,
    ncol = p
  )

  direction_type <- character(
    number_directions
  )

  current_direction <- 1L

  # Dense directions inspect combinations involving every tensor entry.
  if (n_dense > 0L) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_dense)) {
      direction <- rnorm(p)
      direction <- direction /
        sqrt(sum(direction^2))

      directions[current_direction, ] <-
        direction

      direction_type[current_direction] <-
        "dense"

      current_direction <-
        current_direction + 1L
    }
  }

  # A rank-one direction has the form
  #
  #   u_1 outer u_2 outer ... outer u_D.
  #
  # It examines a combination of the tensor modes while preserving the
  # multilinear structure.
  if (n_rank_one > 0L) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_rank_one)) {
      mode_vectors <- vector(
        "list",
        number_modes
      )

      for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
        mode_vector <- rnorm(
          tensor_dim[mode]
        )

        mode_vector <- mode_vector /
          sqrt(sum(mode_vector^2))

        mode_vectors[[mode]] <-
          mode_vector
      }

      direction_array <-
        mode_vectors[[1L]]

      if (number_modes > 1L) {
        for (mode in 2:number_modes) {
          direction_array <- outer(
            direction_array,
            mode_vectors[[mode]]
          )
        }
      }

      direction <- as.numeric(
        direction_array
      )

      direction <- direction /
        sqrt(sum(direction^2))

      directions[current_direction, ] <-
        direction

      direction_type[current_direction] <-
        "rank_one"

      current_direction <-
        current_direction + 1L
    }
  }

  # Sparse directions examine individual standardized tensor entries. They
  # can detect marginal skewness or tail behavior that a dense random
  # projection may average away.
  if (n_sparse > 0L) {
    sparse_entries <- sample.int(
      p,
      size = n_sparse,
      replace = n_sparse > p
    )

    sparse_signs <- sample(
      c(-1, 1),
      size = n_sparse,
      replace = TRUE
    )

    for (j in seq_len(n_sparse)) {
      directions[
        current_direction,
        sparse_entries[j]
      ] <- sparse_signs[j]

      direction_type[current_direction] <-
        "sparse"

      current_direction <-
        current_direction + 1L
    }
  }

  # Evaluate every base direction at every radius. Unlike drawing a new
  # direction at each radius, this shows how the CF changes along the same
  # tensor direction at several distances from zero.
  number_frequencies <-
    number_directions * length(radii)

  frequencies <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = number_frequencies,
    ncol = p
  )

  frequency_type <- character(
    number_frequencies
  )

  frequency_radius <- numeric(
    number_frequencies
  )

  current_frequency <- 1L

  for (direction_number in seq_len(number_directions)) {
    for (radius in radii) {
      frequencies[current_frequency, ] <-
        radius *
        directions[direction_number, ]

      frequency_type[current_frequency] <-
        direction_type[direction_number]

      frequency_radius[current_frequency] <-
        radius

      current_frequency <-
        current_frequency + 1L
    }
  }

  rownames(frequencies) <- paste0(
    frequency_type,
    "_r",
    frequency_radius,
    "_",
    seq_len(number_frequencies)
  )

  frequencies
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Simulate the fitted null distribution of the radial distance
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

simulate_fitted_radial_distances <- function(
    n,
    fit,
    model,
    tensor_dim) {

  p <- prod(tensor_dim)

  # After correct normal standardization, the squared Euclidean norm is
  # chi-squared with p degrees of freedom.
  if (model == "normal") {
    return(rchisq(
      n,
      df = p
    ))
  }

  # Transform the skew tensor using the same whitening matrices applied to
  # the observations.
  standardized_skew <- fit$skew

  for (mode in seq_along(fit$sigmas)) {
    sigma <- as.matrix(
      fit$sigmas[[mode]]
    )

    sigma <- (
      sigma + t(sigma)
    ) / 2

    whitening <- solve(
      t(chol(sigma))
    )

    standardized_skew <- n_prod(
      standardized_skew,
      mode,
      whitening
    )
  }

  skew_length_squared <- sum(
    as.numeric(standardized_skew)^2
  )

  # Draw only the scalar mixing variables. There is no need to simulate full
  # tensors to obtain the radial reference distribution.
  if (model == "skewt") {
    W <- invgamma::rinvgamma(
      n,
      shape = fit$nu / 2,
      rate = fit$nu / 2
    )
  }

  if (model == "vargamma") {
    W <- rgamma(
      n,
      shape = fit$gamma,
      rate = fit$gamma
    )
  }

  if (model == "invgauss") {
    W <- statmod::rinvgauss(
      n,
      mean = 1 / fit$kappa,
      shape = 1
    )
  }

  if (model == "genhyper") {
    W <- GIGrvg::rgig(
      n,
      lambda = fit$lambda,
      chi = fit$omega,
      psi = fit$omega
    )
  }

  # Conditional on W,
  #
  #   ||Z||^2 / W
  #
  # is noncentral chi-squared with noncentrality W ||A||^2.
  W * rchisq(
    n,
    df = p,
    ncp = W * skew_length_squared
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Calculate an Anderson-Darling radial discrepancy
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_radial_discrepancy <- function(
    radial_distances,
    fit,
    model,
    tensor_dim,
    n_radial_reference = 50000L) {

  n <- length(radial_distances)
  p <- prod(tensor_dim)

  if (model == "normal") {
    # The normal radial CDF is known exactly.
    null_cdf <- pchisq(
      radial_distances,
      df = p
    )
  } else {
    # For a skewed variance mixture, approximate the one-dimensional radial
    # CDF using inexpensive scalar simulations.
    reference_radial <- simulate_fitted_radial_distances(
      n = n_radial_reference,
      fit = fit,
      model = model,
      tensor_dim = tensor_dim
    )

    reference_radial <- sort(
      reference_radial
    )

    null_cdf <- findInterval(
      radial_distances,
      reference_radial
    ) / n_radial_reference
  }

  # Avoid log(0) in the Anderson-Darling formula.
  lower_bound <- 1 / (
    n_radial_reference + 1
  )

  null_cdf <- pmin(
    1 - lower_bound,
    pmax(lower_bound, null_cdf)
  )

  null_cdf <- sort(
    null_cdf
  )

  index <- seq_len(n)

  # Large values indicate that the observed radial distribution differs from
  # the fitted model, with extra emphasis on the two tails.
  -n - sum(
    (2 * index - 1) *
      (
        log(null_cdf) +
          log(1 - rev(null_cdf))
      )
  ) / n
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Calculate the projection and radial components for one fitted model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

calculate_omnibus_cf_components <- function(
    draws,
    fit,
    model,
    frequencies,
    n_radial_reference = 50000L,
    covariance_ridge = 1e-8) {

  n <- n_draws(draws)
  tensor_dim <- draw_shape(draws)
  frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)
  number_frequencies <- nrow(frequencies)

  standardized <- standardize_cf_draws(
    draws = draws,
    fit = fit
  )

  phases <- standardized %*%
    t(frequencies)

  empirical_cf <- colMeans(
    exp(1i * phases)
  )

  theoretical_cf <- theoretical_standardized_cf(
    frequencies = frequencies,
    fit = fit,
    model = model
  )

  # The covariance of cos(t'X) and sin(t'X) can be calculated from phi(t)
  # and phi(2t), so it is unnecessary to estimate a large covariance matrix.
  doubled_theoretical_cf <-
    theoretical_standardized_cf(
      frequencies = 2 * frequencies,
      fit = fit,
      model = model
    )

  projection_statistics <- numeric(
    number_frequencies
  )

  for (j in seq_len(number_frequencies)) {
    cosine_mean <- Re(
      theoretical_cf[j]
    )

    sine_mean <- Im(
      theoretical_cf[j]
    )

    cosine_second_moment <- (
      1 + Re(doubled_theoretical_cf[j])
    ) / 2

    sine_second_moment <- (
      1 - Re(doubled_theoretical_cf[j])
    ) / 2

    cosine_sine_moment <- Im(
      doubled_theoretical_cf[j]
    ) / 2

    feature_covariance <- matrix(
      c(
        cosine_second_moment - cosine_mean^2,
        cosine_sine_moment - cosine_mean * sine_mean,
        cosine_sine_moment - cosine_mean * sine_mean,
        sine_second_moment - sine_mean^2
      ),
      nrow = 2,
      byrow = TRUE
    )

    # The ridge only protects against an almost singular 2 by 2 covariance
    # at frequencies very close to zero.
    feature_covariance <- feature_covariance +
      diag(covariance_ridge, 2)

    difference <- c(
      Re(
        empirical_cf[j] -
          theoretical_cf[j]
      ),
      Im(
        empirical_cf[j] -
          theoretical_cf[j]
      )
    )

    projection_statistics[j] <- n *
      drop(
        t(difference) %*%
          solve(
            feature_covariance,
            difference
          )
      )
  }

  # The maximum retains a discrepancy that occurs along only one or a few
  # informative tensor directions instead of averaging it away.
  projection_maximum <- max(
    projection_statistics
  )

  radial_distances <- rowSums(
    standardized^2
  )

  radial_statistic <- calculate_radial_discrepancy(
    radial_distances = radial_distances,
    fit = fit,
    model = model,
    tensor_dim = tensor_dim,
    n_radial_reference = n_radial_reference
  )

  list(
    projection = projection_maximum,
    radial = radial_statistic,
    projection_statistics = projection_statistics,
    radial_distances = radial_distances,
    empirical_cf = empirical_cf,
    theoretical_cf = theoretical_cf
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Run the complete omnibus parametric-bootstrap test
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gof_characteristic_omnibus <- function(
    draws,
    model = c(
      "normal",
      "skewt",
      "vargamma",
      "invgauss",
      "genhyper"
    ),
    B = 199L,
    frequencies = NULL,
    n_dense = 25L,
    n_rank_one = 25L,
    n_sparse = 25L,
    radii = c(0.5, 1, 2),
    n_radial_reference = 50000L,
    covariance_ridge = 1e-8,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-6,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    seed = NULL,
    show_progress = TRUE) {

  model <- match.arg(model)
  data_name <- deparse(substitute(draws))

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a tensor object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  B <- as.integer(B)

  if (B < 2L) {
    stop(
      "`B` must be at least 2.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  n <- n_draws(draws)

  # Fit the model to the observed tensors.
  observed_fit <- tensor_mle(
    draws,
    model = model,
    max_iter = max_iter,
    tol = tol,
    quiet = quiet,
    restrict = restrict
  )

  # Generate one frequency set and hold it fixed throughout the bootstrap.
  # Because these directions are random rather than selected from the
  # observed CF discrepancies, fixing them does not search for a favorable
  # observed p-value.
  if (is.null(frequencies)) {
    frequencies <- make_omnibus_cf_frequencies(
      tensor_dim = draw_shape(draws),
      n_dense = n_dense,
      n_rank_one = n_rank_one,
      n_sparse = n_sparse,
      radii = radii
    )
  } else {
    frequencies <- as.matrix(
      frequencies
    )
  }

  observed_components <-
    calculate_omnibus_cf_components(
      draws = draws,
      fit = observed_fit,
      model = model,
      frequencies = frequencies,
      n_radial_reference = n_radial_reference,
      covariance_ridge = covariance_ridge
    )

  # Column 1 stores the maximum studentized CF discrepancy. Column 2 stores
  # the radial Anderson-Darling discrepancy.
  bootstrap_components <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = 2,
    dimnames = list(
      NULL,
      c("projection", "radial")
    )
  )

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    bootstrap_draws <- simulate_cf_reference_draws(
      n = n,
      fit = observed_fit,
      model = model
    )

    # Refitting makes the bootstrap reproduce the complete fitted-model
    # procedure. A failed skewed-model optimization is recorded as NA.
    bootstrap_fit <- tryCatch(
      tensor_mle(
        bootstrap_draws,
        model = model,
        max_iter = max_iter,
        tol = tol,
        quiet = quiet,
        restrict = restrict
      ),
      error = function(error) NULL
    )

    if (!is.null(bootstrap_fit)) {
      current_components <- tryCatch(
        calculate_omnibus_cf_components(
          draws = bootstrap_draws,
          fit = bootstrap_fit,
          model = model,
          frequencies = frequencies,
          n_radial_reference = n_radial_reference,
          covariance_ridge = covariance_ridge
        ),
        error = function(error) NULL
      )

      if (!is.null(current_components) &&
          is.finite(current_components$projection) &&
          is.finite(current_components$radial)) {
        bootstrap_components[b, ] <- c(
          current_components$projection,
          current_components$radial
        )
      }
    }

    if (show_progress &&
        (b %% 25L == 0L || b == B)) {
      message(
        "Completed ",
        b,
        " of ",
        B,
        " omnibus bootstrap samples."
      )
    }
  }

  successful <- apply(
    bootstrap_components,
    1,
    function(current_row) {
      all(is.finite(current_row))
    }
  )

  number_successful <- sum(
    successful
  )

  number_failed <- B -
    number_successful

  if (number_successful < 2L) {
    stop(
      "Fewer than two bootstrap fits succeeded.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (number_failed > 0L) {
    warning(
      number_failed,
      " of ",
      B,
      " omnibus bootstrap fits failed. The p-value uses the ",
      number_successful,
      " successful fits.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  successful_components <- bootstrap_components[
    successful,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  observed_component_vector <- c(
    projection = observed_components$projection,
    radial = observed_components$radial
  )

  # The projection maximum and radial statistic have different numerical
  # scales. Standardize each using its bootstrap null mean and standard
  # deviation before taking their maximum.
  component_center <- colMeans(
    successful_components
  )

  component_scale <- apply(
    successful_components,
    2,
    sd
  )

  if (any(!is.finite(component_scale)) ||
      any(component_scale <= 0)) {
    stop(
      "A bootstrap component has zero or non-finite variation.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  observed_standardized <- (
    observed_component_vector -
      component_center
  ) / component_scale

  bootstrap_standardized <- sweep(
    successful_components,
    2,
    component_center,
    "-"
  )

  bootstrap_standardized <- sweep(
    bootstrap_standardized,
    2,
    component_scale,
    "/"
  )

  # The omnibus statistic is large when either the projection component or
  # radial component is unusually large.
  observed_omnibus <- max(
    observed_standardized
  )

  bootstrap_omnibus <- apply(
    bootstrap_standardized,
    1,
    max
  )

  p_value <- (
    1 + sum(
      bootstrap_omnibus >= observed_omnibus
    )
  ) / (
    number_successful + 1
  )

  # Component p-values help explain whether rejection came from a particular
  # projection or from the radial/tail behavior.
  projection_p_value <- (
    1 + sum(
      successful_components[, "projection"] >=
        observed_component_vector["projection"]
    )
  ) / (
    number_successful + 1
  )

  radial_p_value <- (
    1 + sum(
      successful_components[, "radial"] >=
        observed_component_vector["radial"]
    )
  ) / (
    number_successful + 1
  )

  structure(
    list(
      statistic = c(T = observed_omnibus),
      p.value = p_value,
      method = paste(
        "Omnibus parametric-bootstrap tensor CF test for",
        model
      ),
      data.name = data_name,
      model = model,
      fit = observed_fit,
      frequencies = frequencies,
      observed_components = observed_component_vector,
      standardized_components = observed_standardized,
      component_p_values = c(
        projection = projection_p_value,
        radial = radial_p_value
      ),
      projection_statistics =
        observed_components$projection_statistics,
      radial_distances =
        observed_components$radial_distances,
      empirical_cf =
        observed_components$empirical_cf,
      theoretical_cf =
        observed_components$theoretical_cf,
      bootstrap_components = bootstrap_components,
      bootstrap_statistics = bootstrap_omnibus,
      component_center = component_center,
      component_scale = component_scale,
      B = B,
      successful_bootstraps = number_successful,
      failed_bootstraps = number_failed
    ),
    class = "htest"
  )
}
```

The function below calculates the score matrix for a tensor variate normal of
any shape. The \(2\times2\) model is used only for the example following the
function. For identifiability, `tensor_mle()` fixes the trace of every
covariance factor except the last one. The covariance perturbations below
preserve those trace constraints.

```{r tvn-score-information}
# Calculate one score row per tensor draw for a fitted TVN model.
#
# Column j approximates the derivative of each draw's log density with
# respect to one locally free fitted parameter. We use the finite difference
#
#   {log f(theta + step) - log f(theta - step)} / (2 * step).
#
# `restrict` optionally lists covariance modes that were fixed when fitting.
score_matrix <- function(draws, fit, finite_difference = 1e-5, restrict = NULL) {
  dims <- draw_shape(draws)
  number_modes <- length(dims)
  p <- prod(dims)
  n <- n_draws(draws)

  if (length(fit$sigmas) != number_modes) {
    stop("The fitted covariance factors do not match the tensor shape.")
  }

  # Each entry records one valid direction in which a fitted parameter
  # can be moved.
  directions <- list()

  for (j in seq_len(p)) { #store each mu value as a parameter
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "mu",
      index = j,
      name = paste0("mu[", j, "]"),
      scale = max(1, abs(as.numeric(fit$mu)[j]))
    )
  }

  # Create the free symmetric directions for every covariance factor.
  for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
    if (mode %in% restrict) {
      next
    }

    mode_size <- dims[mode]
    sigma_mode <- fit$sigmas[[mode]]
    covariance_scale <- max(1, sqrt(mean(sigma_mode^2)))

    if (mode < number_modes && mode_size > 1L) {
      # The trace of this covariance is fixed. Increasing one diagonal
      # entry while decreasing the last preserves the trace.
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size - 1L)) {
        direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
        direction_matrix[row, row] <- 1
        direction_matrix[mode_size, mode_size] <- -1

        directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
          type = "sigma",
          mode = mode,
          matrix = direction_matrix,
          name = paste0("sigma", mode, "_diag_", row),
          scale = covariance_scale
        )
      }
    } else {
      # The last covariance factor is unrestricted.
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size)) {
        direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
        direction_matrix[row, row] <- 1

        directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
          type = "sigma",
          mode = mode,
          matrix = direction_matrix,
          name = paste0("sigma", mode, "_diag_", row),
          scale = covariance_scale
        )
      }
    }

    # A symmetric off-diagonal pair is one free parameter.
    if (mode_size > 1L) {
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size - 1L)) {
        for (column in seq.int(row + 1L, mode_size)) {
          direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
          direction_matrix[row, column] <- 1
          direction_matrix[column, row] <- 1

          directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
            type = "sigma",
            mode = mode,
            matrix = direction_matrix,
            name = paste0(
              "sigma", mode, "_offdiag_", row, "_", column
            ),
            scale = covariance_scale
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  number_parameters <- length(directions)
  scores <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n, ncol = number_parameters)

  # Move the fitted model a small distance in one parameter direction.
  perturb_fit <- function(direction, amount) {
    candidate <- fit

    if (direction$type == "mu") {
      candidate_mu <- as.numeric(candidate$mu)
      candidate_mu[direction$index] <-
        candidate_mu[direction$index] + amount
      candidate$mu <- array(candidate_mu, dim = dims)
    }

    if (direction$type == "sigma") {
      mode <- direction$mode
      candidate$sigmas[[mode]] <-
        candidate$sigmas[[mode]] + amount * direction$matrix
    }

    candidate
  }

  for (j in seq_len(number_parameters)) {
    direction <- directions[[j]]
    step <- finite_difference * direction$scale
    derivative_found <- FALSE

    # A covariance estimate might be close to the positive-definite
    # boundary. If necessary, reduce the finite-difference step.
    for (attempt in seq_len(12L)) {
      fit_plus <- perturb_fit(direction, step)
      fit_minus <- perturb_fit(direction, -step)

      covariance_ok <- TRUE

      if (direction$type == "sigma") {
        mode <- direction$mode
        covariance_ok <-
          !inherits(
            try(chol(fit_plus$sigmas[[mode]]), silent = TRUE),
            "try-error"
          ) &&
          !inherits(
            try(chol(fit_minus$sigmas[[mode]]), silent = TRUE),
            "try-error"
          )
      }

      if (covariance_ok) {
        log_density_plus <- tryCatch(
          dtnorm(
            draws,
            mu = fit_plus$mu,
            sigmas = fit_plus$sigmas,
            log = TRUE
          ),
          error = function(error) rep(NA_real_, n)
        )

        log_density_minus <- tryCatch(
          dtnorm(
            draws,
            mu = fit_minus$mu,
            sigmas = fit_minus$sigmas,
            log = TRUE
          ),
          error = function(error) rep(NA_real_, n)
        )

        if (all(is.finite(log_density_plus)) &&
            all(is.finite(log_density_minus))) {
          scores[, j] <- (
            log_density_plus - log_density_minus
          ) / (2 * step)

          derivative_found <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }

      step <- step / 2
    }

    if (!derivative_found) {
      stop(
        "Could not calculate the score direction ",
        direction$name,
        "."
      )
    }
  }

  parameter_names <- character(number_parameters)

  for (j in seq_len(number_parameters)) {
    parameter_names[j] <- directions[[j]]$name
  }

  colnames(scores) <- parameter_names

  scores
}

# Demonstration: 100 draws from a 2 x 2 TVN.
tvn_scores <- score_matrix(
  draws = small,
  fit = mle_small
)

# At the exact MLE, the average score is zero. Centering removes small
# deviations caused by optimizer and finite-difference tolerances.
centered_tvn_scores <- sweep(
  tvn_scores,
  MARGIN = 2,
  STATS = colMeans(tvn_scores),
  FUN = "-"
)

# The average outer product of the individual scores estimates the
# per-observation Fisher information matrix.
I_hat <- crossprod(centered_tvn_scores) / n_draws(small)

round(I_hat, 3)
eigen(I_hat, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values

# Estimate the gradient of the CF at frequency s.
#
# For each fitted parameter, average
#
#   observed CF value at s * score for that parameter.
#
# The result has one complex derivative for every column of tvn_scores.
n <- n_draws(small)
p <- prod(draw_shape(small))

small_matrix <- matrix(
  unclass(small),
  nrow = n,
  ncol = p
)

s_vector <- as.numeric(s)
s_angles <- as.vector(small_matrix %*% s_vector)
s_cf_values <- exp(1i * s_angles)
s_cf_values <- s_cf_values - mean(s_cf_values)

gradient_s <- complex(length = ncol(centered_tvn_scores))

for (j in seq_len(ncol(centered_tvn_scores))) {
  gradient_s[j] <- mean(
    s_cf_values * centered_tvn_scores[, j]
  )
}

names(gradient_s) <- colnames(centered_tvn_scores)
gradient_s

# Repeat the same calculation at frequency t.
t_vector <- as.numeric(t)
t_angles <- as.vector(small_matrix %*% t_vector)
t_cf_values <- exp(1i * t_angles)
t_cf_values <- t_cf_values - mean(t_cf_values)

gradient_t <- complex(length = ncol(centered_tvn_scores))

for (j in seq_len(ncol(centered_tvn_scores))) {
  gradient_t[j] <- mean(
    t_cf_values * centered_tvn_scores[, j]
  )
}

names(gradient_t) <- colnames(centered_tvn_scores)
gradient_t

# This is the fitted-parameter correction for the covariance between the
# CF differences at s and t.
mle_correction_st <- sum(
  gradient_s * solve(I_hat, Conj(gradient_t))
)
```

The function below creates frequencies in a standardized reference space. It
first generates random directions with Frobenius norm one, and then evaluates
each direction at several distances from zero. The default radii cover regions
where the standardized normal characteristic function is large, intermediate,
small, and nearly zero.

```{r}
make_reference_freq <- function(
    tensor_dim,
    n_directions = 50,
    radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
    seed = 1) {

  # Use a seed so that the same inputs produce the same frequencies.
  set.seed(seed)

  # p is the number of entries in one tensor.
  p <- prod(tensor_dim)

  # Generate one random direction in R^p for each row.
  direction_matrix <- matrix(
    rnorm(n_directions * p),
    nrow = n_directions,
    ncol = p
  )

  # Scale every direction so that its Frobenius norm is one.
  # After normalization, the direction controls where we look,
  # while the radius below controls how far from zero we look.
  for (j in 1:n_directions) {

    direction_length <- sqrt(
      sum(direction_matrix[j, ]^2)
    )

    direction_matrix[j, ] <-
      direction_matrix[j, ] / direction_length
  }

  # We use every direction once at every requested radius.
  number_frequencies <-
    n_directions * length(radii)

  frequency_matrix <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = number_frequencies,
    ncol = p
  )

  current_row <- 1

  for (radius in radii) {
    for (j in 1:n_directions) {

      frequency_matrix[current_row, ] <-
        radius * direction_matrix[j, ]

      current_row <- current_row + 1
    }
  }

  tensor( #each row is a tensor freq
    data = c(t(frequency_matrix)),
    dim = tensor_dim,
    n = number_frequencies
  )
}
```


First, we define the empirical characteristic function. For any tensor object with independent, identically distributed draws, we can compute the empirical characteristic function. Given a frequency tensor $\mathcal{T}$, we want to compute $E[\exp \{i \text{vec}(\tensor{T})' \text{vec}(\tensor{X})\}]$.

```{r}
emp_cf <- function(draws, frequencies) {
  n <- n_draws(draws)
  L <- n_draws(frequencies)

  p <- prod(draw_shape(draws))

  draw_matrix <- matrix(
    unclass(draws),
    nrow = n,
    ncol = p
  )

  frequency_matrix <- matrix(
    unclass(frequencies),
    nrow = L,
    ncol = p
  )

  phases <- draw_matrix %*% t(frequency_matrix)

  colMeans(exp(1i * phases))
}
```


Next, we define the theoretical characteristic function. For the tensor variate normal, this is $E[\exp \{i \text{vec}(\tensor{T})' \text{vec}(\tensor{X})\}] = \exp\left\{i \text{vec}(\tensor{T})' \tensor{M} - \frac{1}{2} \text{vec}(\tensor{T})' \bigotimes_{d=1}^{D} \Sigma_{d} \text{vec}(\tensor{T}) \right\}$.
```{r}
cftnorm <- function(freq, mu, sigmas) {
  num_freq <- n_draws(freq)
  
  res <- complex(num_freq)
  
  for(i in 1:num_freq) {
    curr_freq <- pull_draw(freq, i)
    
    second_term <- curr_freq
  
    for(d in seq_along(sigmas)) {
      second_term <- n_prod(second_term, d, sigmas[[d]])
    }
  
    first_term <- 1i * sum(curr_freq * mu)
  
    res[i] <- exp(first_term - 1/2 * sum(curr_freq * second_term))
  }
  res
}
```


Now we evaluate the empirical and theoretical characteristic function at a variety of frequencies. 
```{r}
freqs <- make_reference_freq(tensor_dim = c(2, 3, 4))

distances <-
  tibble(freqs,
         emp = emp_cf(norm_draws, freqs),
         theory = cftnorm(freqs, mles$mu, mles$sigmas),
         dist = Mod(emp - theory)^2) 

T_stat <- n_draws(norm_draws) * mean(distances$dist)
```


Now we need to compute the null distribution to see if this test statistic is extreme.
```{r}
compute_eigen <- function(freqs, mu, sigmas) {
  L <- n_draws(freqs)
  
  # Theoretical CF at the original frequencies
  phi <- cftnorm(
    freqs,
    mu = mu,
    sigmas = sigmas
  )
  
  # Theoretical means of the cosine/sine features
  feature_mean <- c(
    Re(phi),
    Im(phi)
  )
  
  # Covariance matrix for the 2L cosine/sine features
  V <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = 2 * L,
    ncol = 2 * L
  )
  
  for (j in seq_len(L)) {
    for (k in seq_len(L)) {
  
      freq_j <- pull_draw(freqs, j)
      freq_k <- pull_draw(freqs, k)
  
      freq_plus <- freq_j + freq_k
      freq_minus <- freq_j - freq_k
  
      phi_plus <- cftnorm(
        freq_plus,
        mu = mu,
        sigmas = sigmas
      )
  
      phi_minus <- cftnorm(
        freq_minus,
        mu = mu,
        sigmas = sigmas
      )
  
      # E[cos_j cos_k]
      V[j, k] <- Re(phi_minus + phi_plus) / 2
  
      # E[sin_j sin_k]
      V[L + j, L + k] <- Re(phi_minus - phi_plus) / 2
  
      # E[cos_j sin_k]
      V[j, L + k] <- Im(phi_plus + Conj(phi_minus)) / 2
  
      # Symmetrize the cross block
      V[L + k, j] <- V[j, L + k]
    }
  }
  
  # Convert second moments into covariances
  V <- V - tcrossprod(feature_mean)
  
  # Remove small numerical asymmetry
  V <- (V + t(V)) / 2
  
  eigen(V / L, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
}

eigen_est <- compute_eigen(freqs, mu = mles$mu, sigmas = mles$sigmas)
eigen_real <- compute_eigen(freqs, mu = mu_true, sigmas = sigmas_true)

tibble(est = eigen_est,
       real = eigen_real) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything()) |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(x = value, y = name, color = name)) +
  theme_minimal()

(eigen_est - eigen_real)^2 |> mean()
```


```{r}
gof_characteristic <- function(draws, model) {
  mles <- tensor_mle(draws, model = model) #compute MLEs
  
  freqs <- make_reference_freq(tensor_dim = dim(draws)) #generate freqs 

  distances <- #compute the 
    tibble(freqs,
           emp = emp_cf(draws, freqs),
           theory = cftnorm(freqs, mles$mu, mles$sigmas),
           dist = Mod(emp - theory)^2) 
  
  T_stat <- n_draws(draws) * mean(distances$dist) #test statistic
  
  #estimate the eigenvalues
  eigen_est <- compute_eigen(freqs, mu = mles$mu, sigmas = mles$sigmas)
  
  n_mixture <- 1e5
  
  mixture_stats <- numeric(n_mixture)
  
  for (j in seq_along(eigen_est)) { #generate distribution
    mixture_stats <- mixture_stats + eigen_est[j] * rchisq(n_mixture, df = 1)
  }
  
  p_value <- mean(mixture_stats >= T_stat)
  
  p_value
}

gof_characteristic_param <- function(draws, mu = mu, sigmas = sigmas) {
  freqs <- make_reference_freq(tensor_dim = dim(draws))

  distances <-
    tibble(freqs,
           emp = emp_cf(draws, freqs),
           theory = cftnorm(freqs, mu, sigmas),
           dist = Mod(emp - theory)^2) 
  
  T_stat <- n_draws(draws) * mean(distances$dist)
  
  eigen_est <- compute_eigen(freqs, mu = mu, sigmas = sigmas)
  
  n_mixture <- 1e5
  
  mixture_stats <- numeric(n_mixture)
  
  for (j in seq_along(eigen_est)) {
    mixture_stats <- mixture_stats + eigen_est[j] * rchisq(n_mixture, df = 1)
  }
  
  p_value <- mean(mixture_stats >= T_stat)
  
  p_value
}
```

# Adjust for Parameters
```{r}
# Compute eigenvalues after accounting for estimated parameters from same sample as goodness of fit test.
# V_adjusted = V - C I^{-1} C'
#
# V is the known-parameter covariance of the cosine/sine features, I is the per-observation information matrix, and C is their covariance with the score.
#
# Scores are calculated by finite differences of this package's own density

compute_eigen_adjusted <- 
  function(draws, freqs, 
           model = c("normal", "skewt", "vargamma", "invgauss", "genhyper"),
           fit = NULL, max_iter = 1000L, tol = 1e-6, quiet = TRUE, 
           restrict = NULL, finite_difference = 1e-5, information_tolerance = 1e-8,
           eigen_tolerance = 1e-10, return_details = FALSE) {
  model <- match.arg(model)

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a tensor object.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  n <- n_draws(draws) #get number of draws and sizes
  dims <- draw_shape(draws)
  number_modes <- length(dims)
  p <- prod(dims)

  if (n < 2L) {
    stop("At least two tensor draws are required.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  # Accept either a tensor containing frequency tensors or an ordinary matrix
  # containing one vectorized frequency in each row.
  if (inherits(freqs, "tensor")) {
    if (!identical(as.integer(draw_shape(freqs)), as.integer(dims))) {
      stop("The frequency tensors must have the same shape as the draws.",
           call. = FALSE)
    }

    frequencies <- matrix(
      unclass(freqs),
      nrow = n_draws(freqs),
      ncol = p
    )
  } else {
    frequencies <- as.matrix(freqs)
  }

  if (ncol(frequencies) != p || nrow(frequencies) < 1L ||
      any(!is.finite(frequencies))) {
    stop(
      "`freqs` must contain finite frequencies with one row per frequency ",
      "and ", p, " columns.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  if (length(finite_difference) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(finite_difference) || finite_difference <= 0) {
    stop("`finite_difference` must be one positive number.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (length(information_tolerance) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(information_tolerance) || information_tolerance <= 0) {
    stop("`information_tolerance` must be one positive number.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (length(eigen_tolerance) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(eigen_tolerance) || eigen_tolerance <= 0) {
    stop("`eigen_tolerance` must be one positive number.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (is.null(fit)) {
    fit <- tensor_mle(draws, model = model, max_iter = max_iter, 
                      tol = tol, quiet = quiet, restrict = restrict)
  }

  needed <- switch( #required params for each model
    model,
    normal = c("mu", "sigmas"),
    skewt = c("mu", "sigmas", "skew", "nu"),
    vargamma = c("mu", "sigmas", "skew", "gamma"),
    invgauss = c("mu", "sigmas", "skew", "kappa"),
    genhyper = c("mu", "sigmas", "skew", "lambda", "omega")
  )

  missing_fit <- setdiff(needed, names(fit))
  if (length(missing_fit)) {
    stop(
      "`fit` is missing: ", paste(missing_fit, collapse = ", "),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  #calculate the known-parameter covariance V using the theoretical CF
  feature_covariance <- .gof_feature_covariance(
    frequencies = frequencies,
    model = model,
    fit = fit
  )
  
  #standardize draws
  standardized <- .gof_standardize_draws(draws, fit)
  phases <- standardized %*% t(frequencies) #mulyiply by freqs
  
  #compute observed cos and sin vals
  feature_values <- cbind(cos(phases), sin(phases)) 

  # A parameter direction describes one locally free coordinate in the fitted
  # model. Covariance directions preserve the package's trace constraints.
  directions <- list()

  for (j in seq_len(p)) {
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "mu",
      index = j,
      name = paste0("mu[", j, "]"),
      scale = max(1, abs(as.numeric(fit$mu)[j]))
    )
  }

  if (model != "normal") {
    for (j in seq_len(p)) {
      directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
        type = "skew",
        index = j,
        name = paste0("skew[", j, "]"),
        scale = max(1, abs(as.numeric(fit$skew)[j]))
      )
    }
  }

  # tensor_mle_normal() fixes covariance factors named in `restrict`.
  # The current skewed-model fitters estimate every covariance factor.
  fixed_modes <- integer(0)
  if (model == "normal" && length(restrict)) {
    fixed_modes <- as.integer(restrict)
  }

  for (mode in seq_len(number_modes)) {
    if (mode %in% fixed_modes) {
      next
    }

    mode_size <- dims[mode]
    sigma_mode <- as.matrix(fit$sigmas[[mode]])
    covariance_scale <- max(1, sqrt(mean(sigma_mode^2)))

    # All but the last covariance factor have trace fixed to their dimension.
    # Diagonal contrasts change one diagonal entry up and the last one down,
    # so the perturbation has trace zero.
    if (mode < number_modes && mode_size > 1L) {
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size - 1L)) {
        direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
        direction_matrix[row, row] <- 1
        direction_matrix[mode_size, mode_size] <- -1

        directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
          type = "sigma",
          mode = mode,
          matrix = direction_matrix,
          name = paste0("sigma", mode, "_diag_contrast_", row),
          scale = covariance_scale
        )
      }
    } else {
      # The last covariance factor is unrestricted, as is the only factor in
      # an ordinary multivariate model.
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size)) {
        direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
        direction_matrix[row, row] <- 1

        directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
          type = "sigma",
          mode = mode,
          matrix = direction_matrix,
          name = paste0("sigma", mode, "_diag_", row),
          scale = covariance_scale
        )
      }
    }

    # A symmetric off-diagonal entry is one free covariance parameter.
    if (mode_size > 1L) {
      for (row in seq_len(mode_size - 1L)) {
        for (column in seq.int(row + 1L, mode_size)) {
          direction_matrix <- matrix(0, mode_size, mode_size)
          direction_matrix[row, column] <- 1
          direction_matrix[column, row] <- 1

          directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
            type = "sigma",
            mode = mode,
            matrix = direction_matrix,
            name = paste0(
              "sigma", mode, "_offdiag_", row, "_", column
            ),
            scale = covariance_scale
          )
        }
      }
    }
  }

  if (model == "skewt") {
    # Perturb log(nu), rather than nu itself, so both finite-difference values
    # are always positive.
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_nu",
      name = "log(nu)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  if (model == "vargamma") {
    # gamma is positive, so perturb it on its logarithmic scale.
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_gamma",
      name = "log(gamma)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  if (model == "invgauss") {
    # kappa is positive, so perturb it on its logarithmic scale.
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_kappa",
      name = "log(kappa)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  if (model == "genhyper") {
    # lambda may be negative, zero, or positive, so use its ordinary scale.
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "lambda",
      name = "lambda",
      scale = max(1, abs(fit$lambda))
    )

    # omega must be positive.
    directions[[length(directions) + 1L]] <- list(
      type = "log_omega",
      name = "log(omega)",
      scale = 1
    )
  }

  number_parameters <- length(directions)
  parameter_names <- character(number_parameters)
  score_matrix <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n, ncol = number_parameters)

  # Make a copy of the fitted parameters moved a small amount in one valid
  # parameter direction.
  perturb_fit <- function(base_fit, direction, amount) {
    candidate <- base_fit

    if (direction$type == "mu") {
      value <- as.numeric(candidate$mu)
      value[direction$index] <- value[direction$index] + amount
      candidate$mu <- array(value, dim = dims)
    }

    if (direction$type == "skew") {
      value <- as.numeric(candidate$skew)
      value[direction$index] <- value[direction$index] + amount
      candidate$skew <- array(value, dim = dims)
    }

    if (direction$type == "sigma") {
      mode <- direction$mode
      candidate$sigmas[[mode]] <-
        candidate$sigmas[[mode]] + amount * direction$matrix
      candidate$sigmas[[mode]] <-
        (candidate$sigmas[[mode]] + t(candidate$sigmas[[mode]])) / 2
    }

    if (direction$type == "log_nu") {
      candidate$nu <- base_fit$nu * exp(amount)
    }

    if (direction$type == "log_gamma") {
      candidate$gamma <- base_fit$gamma * exp(amount)
    }

    if (direction$type == "log_kappa") {
      candidate$kappa <- base_fit$kappa * exp(amount)
    }

    if (direction$type == "lambda") {
      candidate$lambda <- base_fit$lambda + amount
    }

    if (direction$type == "log_omega") {
      candidate$omega <- base_fit$omega * exp(amount)
    }

    candidate
  }

  # Return one log density per observation under a candidate parameter value.
  log_density <- function(candidate) {
    switch(
      model,
      normal = dtnorm(
        draws,
        mu = candidate$mu,
        sigmas = candidate$sigmas,
        log = TRUE
      ),
      skewt = dtskewt(
        draws,
        mu = candidate$mu,
        skew = candidate$skew,
        sigmas = candidate$sigmas,
        nu = candidate$nu,
        log = TRUE
      ),
      vargamma = dtvargamma(
        draws,
        mu = candidate$mu,
        skew = candidate$skew,
        sigmas = candidate$sigmas,
        scale = candidate$gamma,
        log = TRUE
      ),
      invgauss = dtinvgauss(
        draws,
        mu = candidate$mu,
        skew = candidate$skew,
        sigmas = candidate$sigmas,
        kappa = candidate$kappa,
        log = TRUE
      ),
      genhyper = dtgenhyper(
        draws,
        mu = candidate$mu,
        skew = candidate$skew,
        sigmas = candidate$sigmas,
        lambda = candidate$lambda,
        omega = candidate$omega,
        log = TRUE
      )
    )
  }

  # Numerical derivative of each observation's log likelihood. If a
  # covariance perturbation gets too close to the positive-definite boundary,
  # repeatedly halve the step.
  for (j in seq_len(number_parameters)) {
    direction <- directions[[j]]
    parameter_names[j] <- direction$name
    step <- finite_difference * direction$scale
    derivative_found <- FALSE

    for (attempt in seq_len(12L)) {
      fit_plus <- perturb_fit(fit, direction, step)
      fit_minus <- perturb_fit(fit, direction, -step)

      covariance_ok <- TRUE
      if (direction$type == "sigma") {
        mode <- direction$mode
        covariance_ok <-
          !inherits(try(chol(fit_plus$sigmas[[mode]]), silent = TRUE),
                    "try-error") &&
          !inherits(try(chol(fit_minus$sigmas[[mode]]), silent = TRUE),
                    "try-error")
      }

      if (covariance_ok) {
        log_plus <- tryCatch(
          log_density(fit_plus),
          error = function(error) rep(NA_real_, n)
        )
        log_minus <- tryCatch(
          log_density(fit_minus),
          error = function(error) rep(NA_real_, n)
        )

        if (length(log_plus) == n && length(log_minus) == n &&
            all(is.finite(log_plus)) && all(is.finite(log_minus))) {
          score_matrix[, j] <- (log_plus - log_minus) / (2 * step)
          derivative_found <- TRUE
          break
        }
      }

      step <- step / 2
    }

    if (!derivative_found) {
      stop(
        "Could not calculate a stable likelihood derivative for ",
        direction$name, ".",
        call. = FALSE
      )
    }
  }

  colnames(score_matrix) <- parameter_names

  # Estimate covariances rather than raw second moments. At an exact MLE the
  # average score is zero, but centering makes this less sensitive to finite
  # optimizer tolerance.
  centered_scores <- sweep(
    score_matrix,
    2,
    colMeans(score_matrix),
    "-"
  )
  centered_features <- sweep(
    feature_values,
    2,
    colMeans(feature_values),
    "-"
  )

  information <- crossprod(centered_scores) / n
  information <- (information + t(information)) / 2

  # Use a symmetric Moore-Penrose inverse. This safely removes score
  # directions that are numerically redundant.
  information_eigen <- eigen(information, symmetric = TRUE)
  largest_information <- max(information_eigen$values, 0)
  information_cutoff <- largest_information * information_tolerance
  keep_information <- information_eigen$values > information_cutoff

  if (!any(keep_information)) {
    stop("The estimated information matrix has numerical rank zero.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (sum(keep_information) < number_parameters) {
    warning(
      "The estimated information matrix has rank ",
      sum(keep_information), " but there are ", number_parameters,
      " fitted parameter directions. The correction uses the identifiable ",
      "score directions only.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  kept_vectors <- information_eigen$vectors[
    , keep_information, drop = FALSE
  ]
  inverse_information <- kept_vectors %*%
    diag(
      1 / information_eigen$values[keep_information],
      nrow = sum(keep_information)
    ) %*%
    t(kept_vectors)

  # C estimates Cov(feature, score). Removing its score projection is the
  # finite-frequency version of the fitted-parameter kernel correction.
  feature_score_covariance <-
    crossprod(centered_features, centered_scores) / n

  parameter_correction <- feature_score_covariance %*%
    inverse_information %*%
    t(feature_score_covariance)

  # The empirical covariance and C I^{-1} C' are estimated from the same
  # observations. Their difference is the covariance of the feature residuals
  # after projecting out the score directions. Calculating it through the
  # residuals guarantees a positive-semidefinite estimate in finite samples.
  #
  # Its probability limit is the theoretical V - C I^{-1} C' correction.
  score_projection <- centered_scores %*%
    inverse_information %*%
    t(feature_score_covariance)
  adjusted_feature_values <- centered_features - score_projection
  adjusted_covariance <- crossprod(adjusted_feature_values) / n
  adjusted_covariance <-
    (adjusted_covariance + t(adjusted_covariance)) / 2

  empirical_feature_covariance <- crossprod(centered_features) / n
  empirical_feature_covariance <-
    (empirical_feature_covariance + t(empirical_feature_covariance)) / 2

  model_based_adjusted_covariance <-
    feature_covariance - parameter_correction
  model_based_adjusted_covariance <-
    (model_based_adjusted_covariance +
       t(model_based_adjusted_covariance)) / 2

  number_frequencies <- nrow(frequencies)
  adjusted_eigen <- eigen(
    adjusted_covariance / number_frequencies,
    symmetric = TRUE,
    only.values = TRUE
  )$values

  largest_adjusted <- max(adjusted_eigen, 0)
  eigen_cutoff <- largest_adjusted * eigen_tolerance
  eigenvalues <- adjusted_eigen[adjusted_eigen > eigen_cutoff]

  if (!length(eigenvalues)) {
    stop("The adjusted feature covariance has numerical rank zero.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  if (!return_details) {
    return(eigenvalues)
  }

  # Detailed output is useful when checking numerical rank or validating the
  # correction in a simulation study.
  list(
    eigenvalues = eigenvalues,
    all_eigenvalues = adjusted_eigen,
    adjusted_feature_covariance = adjusted_covariance,
    unadjusted_feature_covariance = feature_covariance,
    empirical_feature_covariance = empirical_feature_covariance,
    model_based_adjusted_covariance = model_based_adjusted_covariance,
    parameter_correction = parameter_correction,
    information = information,
    information_eigenvalues = information_eigen$values,
    information_rank = sum(keep_information),
    number_parameters = number_parameters,
    parameter_names = parameter_names,
    mean_score = colMeans(score_matrix),
    fit = fit,
    frequencies = frequencies
  )
}
```

# Recommended test: multiscale CF with a parametric bootstrap

This is the primary goodness-of-fit procedure used in this notebook. It tests
the tensor normal and all four skewed variance-mixture models implemented by
`tensor_mle()`: skew-$t$, variance-gamma, inverse-Gaussian, and generalized
hyperbolic. The test uses both dense tensor directions and rank-one tensor
directions at several frequency radii. The same frequencies are retained for
the observed data and every bootstrap sample. Each bootstrap sample is refit,
so the p-value accounts for estimating the null model from the data.

The statistic is

\[
T_n = n\frac{1}{L}\sum_{\ell=1}^L
  \left|\widehat\varphi_n(t_\ell)
  -\varphi(t_\ell;\widehat\theta)\right|^2.
\]

The model CFs below are evaluated analytically. Consequently, the test does
not add Monte Carlo error when evaluating the skewed-model CFs.

```{r recommended-multiscale-cf-functions}
.multiscale_cf_whitening <- function(sigmas) {
  lapply(sigmas, function(sigma) {
    sigma <- as.matrix(sigma)
    sigma <- (sigma + t(sigma)) / 2
    solve(t(chol(sigma)))
  })
}

.multiscale_cf_standardize <- function(draws, fit) {
  n <- n_draws(draws)
  dims <- draw_shape(draws)
  whitening <- .multiscale_cf_whitening(fit$sigmas)
  result <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = prod(dims))

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    current <- pull_draw(draws, i) - fit$mu
    for (mode in seq_along(whitening)) {
      current <- n_prod(current, mode, whitening[[mode]])
    }
    result[i, ] <- as.numeric(unclass(current))
  }

  result
}

.multiscale_cf_rank_one_direction <- function(dims) {
  mode_vectors <- lapply(dims, function(mode_size) {
    direction <- rnorm(mode_size)
    direction / sqrt(sum(direction^2))
  })

  as.numeric(Reduce(
    function(left, right) as.vector(outer(left, right)),
    mode_vectors
  ))
}

# Generate an equal number of dense and rank-one directions at each radius.
# Every row has the radius recorded in its `radius` attribute.
make_multiscale_cf_frequencies <- function(dims,
                                           radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
                                           n_per_type = 8L,
                                           seed = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  if (any(!is.finite(radii)) || any(radii <= 0)) {
    stop("`radii` must contain positive finite values.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (length(n_per_type) != 1L || !is.finite(n_per_type) ||
      n_per_type < 1L || n_per_type != floor(n_per_type)) {
    stop("`n_per_type` must be one positive integer.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  p <- prod(dims)
  n_per_type <- as.integer(n_per_type)
  n_frequencies <- length(radii) * 2L * n_per_type
  frequencies <- matrix(0, nrow = n_frequencies, ncol = p)
  direction_type <- character(n_frequencies)
  frequency_radius <- numeric(n_frequencies)
  row <- 0L

  for (radius in radii) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_per_type)) {
      row <- row + 1L
      dense <- rnorm(p)
      frequencies[row, ] <- radius * dense / sqrt(sum(dense^2))
      direction_type[row] <- "dense"
      frequency_radius[row] <- radius

      row <- row + 1L
      frequencies[row, ] <- radius *
        .multiscale_cf_rank_one_direction(dims)
      direction_type[row] <- "rank-one"
      frequency_radius[row] <- radius
    }
  }

  attr(frequencies, "direction_type") <- direction_type
  attr(frequencies, "radius") <- frequency_radius
  frequencies
}

.multiscale_cf_whiten_skew <- function(skew, sigmas) {
  whitening <- .multiscale_cf_whitening(sigmas)
  result <- skew

  for (mode in seq_along(whitening)) {
    result <- n_prod(result, mode, whitening[[mode]])
  }

  as.numeric(result)
}

# Laplace transform E[exp(-s W)] for the mixing variable W. In the CF,
# s = ||t||^2 / 2 - i <t, whitened_skew>, whose real part is nonnegative.
.multiscale_cf_mixing_laplace <- function(s, model, fit) {
  if (model == "skewt") {
    shape <- fit$nu / 2
    rate <- fit$nu / 2
    answer <- complex(length(s))
    at_zero <- Mod(s) < sqrt(.Machine$double.eps)
    answer[at_zero] <- 1 + 0i

    if (any(!at_zero)) {
      current_s <- s[!at_zero]
      argument <- 2 * sqrt(rate * current_s)

      # BesselK(..., expon.scaled = TRUE) equals exp(argument) K(argument).
      log_bessel_k <- log(Bessel::BesselK(
        argument,
        nu = shape,
        expon.scaled = TRUE
      )) - argument

      answer[!at_zero] <- exp(
        log(2) +
          (shape / 2) * (log(rate) + log(current_s)) -
          lgamma(shape) +
          log_bessel_k
      )
    }
    return(answer)
  }

  if (model == "vargamma") {
    return((fit$gamma / (fit$gamma + s))^fit$gamma)
  }

  if (model == "invgauss") {
    return(exp(
      fit$kappa * (1 - sqrt(1 + 2 * s / fit$kappa^2))
    ))
  }

  if (model == "genhyper") {
    shifted_psi <- fit$omega + 2 * s
    argument <- sqrt(fit$omega * shifted_psi)

    log_numerator_bessel <- log(Bessel::BesselK(
      argument,
      nu = fit$lambda,
      expon.scaled = TRUE
    )) - argument
    log_denominator_bessel <- log(Bessel::BesselK(
      fit$omega,
      nu = fit$lambda,
      expon.scaled = TRUE
    )) - fit$omega

    return(exp(
      (fit$lambda / 2) * (log(fit$omega) - log(shifted_psi)) +
        log_numerator_bessel - log_denominator_bessel
    ))
  }

  stop("No mixing distribution is required for the normal model.",
       call. = FALSE)
}

.multiscale_cf_model <- function(frequencies, model, fit) {
  q <- rowSums(frequencies^2)

  if (model == "normal") {
    return(exp(-q / 2))
  }

  whitened_skew <- .multiscale_cf_whiten_skew(
    fit$skew,
    fit$sigmas
  )
  skew_projection <- drop(frequencies %*% whitened_skew)
  s <- q / 2 - 1i * skew_projection

  .multiscale_cf_mixing_laplace(s, model, fit)
}

.multiscale_cf_statistic <- function(draws, model, fit, frequencies) {
  standardized <- .multiscale_cf_standardize(draws, fit)
  phases <- standardized %*% t(frequencies)
  empirical_cf <- colMeans(exp(1i * phases))
  theoretical_cf <- .multiscale_cf_model(frequencies, model, fit)

  if (any(!is.finite(theoretical_cf))) {
    stop("The fitted model produced a non-finite characteristic function.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  squared_difference <- Mod(empirical_cf - theoretical_cf)^2

  list(
    statistic = n_draws(draws) * mean(squared_difference),
    empirical_cf = empirical_cf,
    theoretical_cf = theoretical_cf,
    squared_difference = squared_difference
  )
}

.multiscale_cf_simulate <- function(n, model, fit) {
  switch(
    model,
    normal = rtnorm(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas
    ),
    skewt = rtskewt(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      skew = fit$skew,
      nu = fit$nu
    ),
    vargamma = rtvargamma(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      skew = fit$skew,
      scale = fit$gamma
    ),
    invgauss = rtinvgauss(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      skew = fit$skew,
      kappa = fit$kappa
    ),
    genhyper = rtgenhyper(
      n = n,
      mu = fit$mu,
      sigmas = fit$sigmas,
      skew = fit$skew,
      lambda = fit$lambda,
      omega = fit$omega
    )
  )
}

tensor_cf_multiscale_bootstrap <- function(
    draws,
    model = c("normal", "skewt", "vargamma", "invgauss", "genhyper"),
    B = 999L,
    frequencies = NULL,
    radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
    n_per_type = 8L,
    max_iter = 1000L,
    tol = 1e-4,
    quiet = TRUE,
    restrict = NULL,
    seed = NULL,
    show_progress = FALSE) {
  model <- match.arg(model)
  data_name <- deparse(substitute(draws))

  if (!inherits(draws, "tensor")) {
    stop("`draws` must be a tensor object.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (n_draws(draws) < 2L) {
    stop("At least two tensor draws are required.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (length(B) != 1L || !is.finite(B) ||
      B < 1L || B != floor(B)) {
    stop("`B` must be one positive integer.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  B <- as.integer(B)
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    set.seed(seed)
  }

  p <- prod(draw_shape(draws))
  if (is.null(frequencies)) {
    frequencies <- make_multiscale_cf_frequencies(
      dims = draw_shape(draws),
      radii = radii,
      n_per_type = n_per_type
    )
  } else {
    frequency_attributes <- attributes(frequencies)[
      c("direction_type", "radius")
    ]
    frequencies <- as.matrix(frequencies)
    if (ncol(frequencies) != p) {
      stop("`frequencies` must have ", p, " columns.", call. = FALSE)
    }
    attributes(frequencies)[names(frequency_attributes)] <-
      frequency_attributes
  }

  observed_fit <- tensor_mle(
    draws,
    model = model,
    max_iter = max_iter,
    tol = tol,
    quiet = quiet,
    restrict = restrict
  )
  observed <- .multiscale_cf_statistic(
    draws,
    model,
    observed_fit,
    frequencies
  )

  bootstrap_statistics <- rep(NA_real_, B)
  failure_messages <- character(B)

  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    if (show_progress) {
      message("Bootstrap replicate ", b, " of ", B, " for ", model)
    }

    bootstrap_result <- tryCatch({
      bootstrap_draws <- .multiscale_cf_simulate(
        n_draws(draws),
        model,
        observed_fit
      )
      bootstrap_fit <- tensor_mle(
        bootstrap_draws,
        model = model,
        max_iter = max_iter,
        tol = tol,
        quiet = quiet,
        restrict = restrict
      )
      .multiscale_cf_statistic(
        bootstrap_draws,
        model,
        bootstrap_fit,
        frequencies
      )
    }, error = function(error) error)

    if (inherits(bootstrap_result, "error")) {
      failure_messages[b] <- conditionMessage(bootstrap_result)
    } else if (is.finite(bootstrap_result$statistic)) {
      bootstrap_statistics[b] <- bootstrap_result$statistic
    } else {
      failure_messages[b] <- "The bootstrap statistic was non-finite."
    }
  }

  successful <- is.finite(bootstrap_statistics)
  if (!any(successful)) {
    stop("All bootstrap replicates failed.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  p_value <- (
    1 + sum(bootstrap_statistics[successful] >= observed$statistic)
  ) / (1 + sum(successful))

  model_label <- c(
    normal = "tensor normal",
    skewt = "tensor skew-t",
    vargamma = "tensor variance-gamma",
    invgauss = "tensor inverse-Gaussian",
    genhyper = "tensor generalized hyperbolic"
  )[[model]]

  structure(
    list(
      statistic = c(T = observed$statistic),
      parameter = c(B = sum(successful)),
      p.value = p_value,
      method = paste0(
        "Parametric-bootstrap multiscale CF test for the ",
        model_label
      ),
      data.name = data_name,
      model = model,
      fit = observed_fit,
      frequencies = frequencies,
      empirical_cf = observed$empirical_cf,
      theoretical_cf = observed$theoretical_cf,
      squared_difference = observed$squared_difference,
      bootstrap_statistics = bootstrap_statistics,
      B_requested = B,
      B_successful = sum(successful),
      B_failed = sum(!successful),
      failure_messages = failure_messages[!successful]
    ),
    class = c("tensor_cf_bootstrap_test", "htest")
  )
}
```

The following chunk applies the test to the same data under all five fitted
models. It is not evaluated automatically because `B = 999` requires 4,995
model refits. Using one shared frequency matrix makes the five diagnostics
directly comparable. Their p-values assess each model separately; they are not
scores for ranking the models.

```{r recommended-all-model-bootstrap, eval=FALSE}
grabmyo_tensors <- readRDS("grabmyo_session1_tensors_16x28x16.rds")
grabmyo_draws <- as_tensor(simplify2array(grabmyo_tensors), obs = 4)

models <- c("normal", "skewt", "vargamma", "invgauss", "genhyper")
model_names <- c(
  normal = "Tensor normal",
  skewt = "Tensor skew-t",
  vargamma = "Tensor variance-gamma",
  invgauss = "Tensor inverse-Gaussian",
  genhyper = "Tensor generalized hyperbolic"
)

shared_frequencies <- make_multiscale_cf_frequencies(
  dims = draw_shape(grabmyo_draws),
  radii = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3),
  n_per_type = 8,
  seed = 20260722
)

all_model_cf_tests <- setNames(
  lapply(models, function(current_model) {
    tensor_cf_multiscale_bootstrap(
      grabmyo_draws,
      model = current_model,
      B = 999,
      frequencies = shared_frequencies,
      max_iter = 1000,
      tol = 1e-4,
      seed = 20260722,
      show_progress = TRUE
    )
  }),
  models
)

all_model_cf_results <- data.frame(
  Model = unname(model_names[models]),
  Statistic = vapply(
    all_model_cf_tests,
    function(test) unname(test$statistic),
    numeric(1)
  ),
  p.value = vapply(
    all_model_cf_tests,
    function(test) test$p.value,
    numeric(1)
  ),
  Successful = vapply(
    all_model_cf_tests,
    function(test) test$B_successful,
```

```{r}
  tibble(real = Re(res), img = Im(res))

  tibble(real = Re(res), img = Im(res))
```

```{r}
tensor_ecf <- function(draws, freq) {
  num_draws <- n_draws(draws)
  num_freq <- n_draws(freq)
  nstar <- prod(draw_shape(draws))

  #each row is a vectorized tensor obs
  draw_matrix <- matrix(unclass(draws),
                        nrow = num_draws,
                        ncol = nstar)

  empirical_cf <- complex(num_freq)

  for (j in 1:num_freq) { #get empirical cf for each freq
    # pull_draw() works consistently for one or many frequencies.
    curr_freq <- pull_draw(freq, j)

    #compute 1 inner prod for each obs
    phases <- drop(draw_matrix %*% c(curr_freq))

    #average cf
    empirical_cf[j] <- mean(cos(phases)) + 1i * mean(sin(phases))
  }

  empirical_cf
}
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

make_reference_freq <- function(tensor_dim,
                                num_per_radius = 50) {
  p <- prod(tensor_dim)

  radii <- c(0.5, 1, 2, 3)

  number_frequencies <-
    length(radii) * num_per_radius

  frequency_values <-
    numeric(number_frequencies * p)

  frequency_number <- 0

  for (radius in radii) {

    for (j in 1:num_per_radius) {

      frequency_number <-
        frequency_number + 1

      # Generate a direction
      direction <- rnorm(p)

      # Make its length exactly one
      direction <-
        direction /
        sqrt(sum(direction^2))

      # Give it the desired distance from zero
      current_frequency <-
        radius * direction

      # Store this frequency
      first_position <-
        (frequency_number - 1) * p + 1

      last_position <-
        frequency_number * p

      frequency_values[
        first_position:last_position
      ] <- current_frequency
    }
  }

  tensor(
    data = frequency_values,
    dim = tensor_dim,
    n = number_frequencies
  )
}
```

```{r raw-scale-cf-statistic}
# Generate frequencies on a reference scale. These have norms
# 0.5, 1, 2, and 3, regardless of the dimensions of a tensor draw.
reference_freq <- make_reference_freq(
  tensor_dim = draw_shape(norm_draws),
  num_per_radius = 50,
  seed = 123
)

# Keep the observations on their original scale. Instead, transform only the
# frequencies so that they account for the fitted mode covariance matrices.
freq <- reference_freq

for (d in seq_along(mle_norm$sigmas)) {
  frequency_transform <- solve(chol(mle_norm$sigmas[[d]]))

  freq <- n_prod(
    freq,
    d, 
    frequency_transform
  )
}

# Compare the theoretical and empirical CFs at the transformed frequencies.
cf_tibble <- tibble::tibble(
  freq = freq,
  cf_theory = cftnorm(
    freq,
    mu = mle_norm$mu,
    sigmas = mle_norm$sigmas
  ),
  cf_emp = tensor_ecf(
    norm_draws,
    freq
  ),
  diff = Mod(cf_theory - cf_emp)
)

# The test statistic is n times the mean SQUARED CF difference.
stat <- n_draws(norm_draws) * mean(cf_tibble$diff^2)

stat
```

```{r}
L <- n_draws(freq)

# Each frequency contributes one cosine feature and one sine feature.
number_features <- 2 * L

# The means of the cosine features are Re(phi), and the means of the sine
# features are Im(phi).
phi <- cf_tibble$cf_theory
feature_mean <- c(Re(phi), Im(phi))

# This matrix will contain E[feature_a * feature_b].
second_moment <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = number_features,
  ncol = number_features
)

for (j in 1:L) {
  freq_j <- pull_draw(freq, j)

  for (k in 1:L) {
    freq_k <- pull_draw(freq, k)

    freq_plus <- freq_j + freq_k
    freq_j_minus_k <- freq_j - freq_k
    freq_k_minus_j <- freq_k - freq_j

    # The product-to-sum formulas require the fitted CF at the sum and
    # differences of each pair of frequencies.
    phi_plus <- cftnorm(
      freq_plus,
      mu = mle_norm$mu,
      sigmas = mle_norm$sigmas
    )
    phi_j_minus_k <- cftnorm(
      freq_j_minus_k,
      mu = mle_norm$mu,
      sigmas = mle_norm$sigmas
    )
    phi_k_minus_j <- cftnorm(
      freq_k_minus_j,
      mu = mle_norm$mu,
      sigmas = mle_norm$sigmas
    )

    # E[cos(t_j'X) cos(t_k'X)]
    second_moment[j, k] <-
      Re(phi_j_minus_k + phi_plus) / 2

    # E[sin(t_j'X) sin(t_k'X)]
    second_moment[L + j, L + k] <-
      Re(phi_j_minus_k - phi_plus) / 2

    # E[cos(t_j'X) sin(t_k'X)]
    second_moment[j, L + k] <-
      Im(phi_plus + phi_k_minus_j) / 2

    # The second-moment matrix is symmetric.
    second_moment[L + k, j] <-
      second_moment[j, L + k]
  }
}

# Convert second moments to covariances:
# Cov(A, B) = E[A * B] - E[A] * E[B].
feature_covariance <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = number_features,
  ncol = number_features
)

for (a in 1:number_features) {
  for (b in 1:number_features) {
    feature_covariance[a, b] <-
      second_moment[a, b] -
      feature_mean[a] * feature_mean[b]
  }
}

# Remove tiny numerical asymmetry before calling eigen().
feature_covariance <-
  (feature_covariance + t(feature_covariance)) / 2

eigen_result <- eigen(
  feature_covariance / L,
  symmetric = TRUE,
  only.values = TRUE
)

all_lambda <- eigen_result$values

cutoff <- max(all_lambda) * 1e-10

lambda <- all_lambda[
  all_lambda > cutoff
]
```


```{r vectorized-normal-feature-covariance}
# This is a faster, vectorized version of the preceding covariance calculation.
# It avoids constructing t_j + t_k and t_j - t_k with nested R loops.

L <- n_draws(freq)
p <- prod(draw_shape(freq))

# Rows are frequencies and columns are tensor entries.
reference_matrix <- matrix(
  unclass(reference_freq),
  nrow = L,
  ncol = p
)

raw_frequency_matrix <- matrix(
  unclass(freq),
  nrow = L,
  ncol = p
)

# Squared norm of each reference frequency.
squared_norm <- rowSums(reference_matrix^2)

# Entry (j, k) is the inner product of reference frequencies j and k.
frequency_inner_products <- tcrossprod(reference_matrix)

# Entry (j, k) is ||s_j||^2 + ||s_k||^2.
pair_squared_norm <- outer(
  squared_norm,
  squared_norm,
  "+"
)

# Calculate ||s_j + s_k||^2 and ||s_j - s_k||^2 for every pair.
quadratic_plus <-
  pair_squared_norm +
  2 * frequency_inner_products

quadratic_minus <-
  pair_squared_norm -
  2 * frequency_inner_products

# Remove tiny negative values caused by floating-point rounding.
quadratic_minus <- pmax(quadratic_minus, 0)

# The raw-scale normal CF also contains t' * mu.
mu_vector <- c(mle_norm$mu)

location <- drop(
  raw_frequency_matrix %*% mu_vector
)

location_plus <- outer(
  location,
  location,
  "+"
)

location_minus <- outer(
  location,
  location,
  "-"
)

# Evaluate phi(t_j + t_k) and phi(t_j - t_k) for every pair at once.
phi_plus <- exp(
  1i * location_plus -
  0.5 * quadratic_plus
)

phi_minus <- exp(
  1i * location_minus -
  0.5 * quadratic_minus
)

# Use the product-to-sum identities to form all second moments.
cos_cos_second_moment <-
  (Re(phi_minus) + Re(phi_plus)) / 2

sin_sin_second_moment <-
  (Re(phi_minus) - Re(phi_plus)) / 2

# phi(t_k - t_j) is Conj(phi(t_j - t_k)), which gives the minus sign.
cos_sin_second_moment <-
  (Im(phi_plus) - Im(phi_minus)) / 2

second_moment_vectorized <- rbind(
  cbind(
    cos_cos_second_moment,
    cos_sin_second_moment
  ),
  cbind(
    t(cos_sin_second_moment),
    sin_sin_second_moment
  )
)

# Means of the original cosine and sine features.
phi_original <- exp(
  1i * location -
  0.5 * squared_norm
)

feature_mean_vectorized <- c(
  Re(phi_original),
  Im(phi_original)
)

# Cov(A, B) = E[A * B] - E[A] * E[B].
feature_covariance_vectorized <-
  second_moment_vectorized -
  tcrossprod(feature_mean_vectorized)

feature_covariance_vectorized <-
  (
    feature_covariance_vectorized +
    t(feature_covariance_vectorized)
  ) / 2

eigen_result_vectorized <- eigen(
  feature_covariance_vectorized / L,
  symmetric = TRUE,
  only.values = TRUE
)

all_lambda_vectorized <-
  eigen_result_vectorized$values

cutoff_vectorized <-
  max(all_lambda_vectorized) * 1e-10

lambda_vectorized <- all_lambda_vectorized[
  all_lambda_vectorized > cutoff_vectorized
]

# These should be close to zero when the loop and vectorized calculations agree.
max_covariance_difference <- max(
  abs(
    feature_covariance_vectorized -
    feature_covariance
  )
)

max_eigenvalue_difference <- max(
  abs(
    all_lambda_vectorized -
    all_lambda
  )
)

c(
  max_covariance_difference = max_covariance_difference,
  max_eigenvalue_difference = max_eigenvalue_difference
)

# Use the faster result in the null-distribution calculation below.
feature_covariance <- feature_covariance_vectorized
lambda <- lambda_vectorized
```

```{r}
standardize <- function(draws) {
  mle_draws <- tensor_mle(draws, model = "normal")
  
  #standardize draws with mean and covar
  standard_draws <- draws - mle_draws$mu
  
  num_sigmas <- length(draw_shape(draws))
  
  for(i in 1:num_sigmas) {
    sigma_i <- mle_draws$sigmas[[i]]
    inv_sigma <- solve(t(chol(sigma_i)))
    
    standard_draws <- n_prod(standard_draws, i, inv_sigma)
  }
  standard_draws
}
```
